title: Binance Releases First $6.3B Hack Findings, Reports No Key Leak Evidence
summary: Binance’s initial investigation points to a possible employee laptop compromise behind a security incident with an estimated $6.3 billion impact. The crypto exchange reported no evidence of a wallet private key leak and pledged to cover all losses. Initial Findings Point to Possible Laptop Compromis...
content:
Binance’s initial investigation points to a possible employee laptop compromise behind a security incident with an estimated $6.3 billion impact. The crypto exchange reported no evidence of a wallet private key leak and pledged to cover all losses.

Key Takeaways

  • Deposits and withdrawals were suspended during security checks.
  • Binance said about $3 billion had been frozen onchain so far.
  • The company pledged to cover losses with its user protection fund and corporate funds.

Initial Findings Point to Possible Laptop Compromise

Binance released its first detailed findings on the estimated $6.3 billion hack on Oct. 29, pointing to a possible employee laptop compromise and reporting no evidence of a wallet private key leak.

In its preliminary investigation findings, the company stated: “Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”

On wallet credentials, the exchange stated:

“We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak.”

Asset Freezes Reach $3 Billion as Binance Pledges Coverage

The preliminary account followed hours of scrutiny after analysts detected billions of dollars leaving its wallets, and founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ) described an apparent Binance hack.

Earlier wallet analysis and asset freezes came as analysts tracked as much as $5.8 billion in potentially compromised assets. Binance subsequently provided its own assessment:

“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”

Binance said it engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. Its teams were also working with authorities to confirm the attackers’ identities and bring them to justice. The frozen amount represents restricted assets, not a confirmed total returned to the exchange.

The coverage pledge named the Secure Asset Fund for Users, known as SAFU: “Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe.” A SAFU conversion into bitcoin began in February under a plan to shift $1 billion in stablecoin reserves.

Zhao acknowledged help from industry participants, including competitors, and described an overnight response involving hundreds of employees. He stated: “It hurts, but we will survive.”

Withdrawal Restart Depends on Security Scan

Deposits and withdrawals were temporarily suspended while security checks continued, and Binance revoked the affected address authorization. Binance co-founder and co-CEO Yi He linked the resumption of withdrawals to the scan’s completion, stating: “We will enable withdrawals as soon as the security scan is complete.”

An updated disclosure through Binance’s proof of reserves system was promised after remediation. The company also committed to a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation was complete and the facts fully verified, directing users to official channels for updates and customer support for further questions.

title: Stellar Unveils Thruput With Multi-Million-Transaction Execution Benchmarks
summary: The Stellar Development Foundation introduced Project Thruput on October 28 as a technology preview that changes how a blockchain execution engine can.
content:
TL;DR: The Stellar Development Foundation introduced Project Thruput on October 28 as a technology preview that changes how a blockchain execution engine can handle competing transactions. For investors, the most important distinction is between measured potential and deployed capacity.

The Stellar Development Foundation introduced Project Thruput on October 28 as a technology preview that changes how a blockchain execution engine can handle competing transactions. In its reported tests, single-validator execution capacity rose from roughly 1.18 million payments per second on one machine to about 7.02 million on eight machines. The project is available on FutureNet with open-source material and reproducible benchmarks. These figures concern a controlled component-level measurement; the foundation explicitly says they do not represent end-to-end public network throughput.

The event and the market response

The proposed model is designed to reduce the ordering bottleneck that appears when many transactions touch shared state. Conventional systems may execute independent instructions in parallel but still serialize work involving the same account or data. Thruput aims to scale execution by adding machines even under highly contended workloads. The foundation describes benchmark tests that used a limited set of accounts and measured execution, signatures and relevant engine work. That may be valuable engineering progress, but it remains distinct from consensus, networking, storage and other factors that determine what users experience.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

For investors, the most important distinction is between measured potential and deployed capacity. A seven-million-per-second figure is striking, but the foundation itself limits it to execution inside an experimental environment. Public-blockchain throughput requires more than rapid local computation. It also demands timely consensus and durable data propagation across independent machines. Until those components are tested together at scale, translating the benchmark into a price or adoption forecast for XLM would be speculative.

Scaling distributed software involves trade-offs between performance, operational complexity and assumptions about the machines running it. A controlled benchmark can isolate a promising improvement, but real networks face unreliable links, competing transactions, storage growth and adversarial behavior. The engineering significance of a research preview lies in giving outsiders material they can inspect and challenge. Product teams should avoid building contractual service promises around an experimental component. The gap between an early prototype and dependable production infrastructure is where much of the necessary development work remains.

A blockchain performance number has to be read alongside the workload and the part of the stack being measured. Execution inside one validator, communication between validators, consensus finality and the performance seen by an application are related but distinct metrics. A breakthrough in one component can enable broader progress without proving that the entire network is ready for the same demand. Independent reproduction and adversarial tests remain important. It is also worth separating the cost of executing a transaction from the resource incentives needed to keep infrastructure functioning at scale.

What the headline does not establish

Another unusual claim is that the model can operate without per-transaction execution fees. Stellar says accounts instead receive a scheduling share related to unlocked native-token balances when demand exceeds capacity, while computational limits still apply to individual transactions. This is an alternative resource-allocation design, not unlimited free infrastructure. It raises questions about fairness, account concentration and protection against abuse. Project Thruput remains a preview, so developers should not mistake its experimental characteristics for the economics or capabilities of Stellar mainnet today.

What to watch next

Independent reproduction of the benchmark, wider workloads and eventual public-network integration are the next meaningful steps. Operators should wait for complete deployment specifications before making promises to users about transaction speed or zero fees.

Primary source: Official statement / source documentation.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin to $1.6 Million: Bitwise Raises Its Long-Term Price Target
summary: Bitwise raised its long-term bitcoin price forecast to $1.6 million by 2036, increasing its projected annual return despite a volatile year. The outlook rests on institutional adoption, limited supply, and growing demand for protection against currency debasement. Bitcoin’s $1.6 Million Target Impli...
content:
Bitwise raised its long-term bitcoin price forecast to $1.6 million by 2036, increasing its projected annual return despite a volatile year. The outlook rests on institutional adoption, limited supply, and growing demand for protection against currency debasement.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitwise raised its target from $1.3 million for 2035 to $1.6 million for 2036.
  • Its valuation assumes bitcoin captures 25% of the gold-and-bitcoin market.
  • The bull scenario projects $3.67 million; the bear scenario puts bitcoin at $130,686.

Bitcoin’s $1.6 Million Target Implies 34.3% Annual Growth

Bitcoin could reach about 19 times its model starting price under a forecast asset manager Bitwise released on Oct. 28. The firm’s base-case forecast, the outcome it considers most likely, puts bitcoin at $1,599,766 by 2036. That implies 34.3% compound annual growth from its Sept. 30 reference price of $83,557.

Last year’s $1.3 million bitcoin target covered the decade through 2035 and implied 28.3% annualized growth. Bitwise attributed the higher projection to expanding markets bitcoin could serve and stronger confidence in its trajectory. The updated outlook follows a roughly 53% decline from bitcoin’s October 2025 high to its June 2026 low.

Head of Research Ryan Rasmussen, a co-author of Bitwise’s report, acknowledged the risks in the company’s bitcoin price forecast announcement:

“Bitcoin will likely remain a volatile asset with sharp downturns, but all signs point to these swings weakening as institutional adoption deepens.”

Gold and Institutional Demand Drive the Valuation

Under the base case, bitcoin captures 25% of a combined gold-and-bitcoin market projected to expand from $31.1 trillion to $109.8 trillion by 2036. Bitwise expects rising government debt and currency debasement to support demand for these assets. Its model also assigns bitcoin 1% of a projected $303.5 trillion institutional investment market, alongside smaller contributions from other uses.

Interviews offered supporting evidence for the adoption thesis: Bitwise’s discussions with 15 institutions found that existing holders maintained their crypto allocations through a roughly 50% market decline between October 2025 and April 2026, while several bought more. Participants included pension funds, endowments, and sovereign wealth funds. Separately, the new outlook projects institutional allocations of 1% to 5% over the decade, implying $1.5 trillion to $7.4 trillion in purchases.

Scarcity underpins the supply calculation, which distributes estimated bitcoin value across its full 21 million supply limit. That includes coins yet to be mined and those assumed lost. The report placed circulating supply at 20.1 million.

Scenarios Put Bitcoin Between $130,686 and $3.67 Million

In the bear scenario, bitcoin reaches $130,686 by 2036, equivalent to 4.6% annualized growth from the reference price. This assumes a 2.5% share of the projected store-of-value market and zero penetration of the other modeled categories.

At the bullish end, a $3,667,911 price implies 46% annualized growth, with bitcoin capturing 50% of the store-of-value market and 5% of institutional investment assets. Higher adoption across other modeled markets also contributes to that scenario.

Technological disruption, including Bitcoin’s future quantum-security risks, and regulatory reversals could undermine these projections. Quantum computing uses quantum physics to perform calculations; sufficiently advanced systems could threaten existing cryptography. Bitwise also identified AI-assisted mathematical advances as a threat. It expects the network will need stronger cryptographic protections, with individual wallets potentially exposed if they fail to migrate.

title: Tim Draper Calls Not Owning Bitcoin ‘Irresponsible,’ Warns of Dollar Shift
summary: Tim Draper warned that businesses could eventually reject dollars in favor of bitcoin, triggering bank runs as demand for fiat currencies erodes. His comments echoed the adoption argument behind his longstanding $250,000 bitcoin forecast. Draper Predicts a Shift From Dollars to Bitcoin Individuals a...
content:
Tim Draper warned that businesses could eventually reject dollars in favor of bitcoin, triggering bank runs as demand for fiat currencies erodes. His comments echoed the adoption argument behind his longstanding $250,000 bitcoin forecast.

Key Takeaways

  • Draper predicted businesses would eventually accept only bitcoin.
  • His $250,000 target dates to 2018 and has missed earlier deadlines.
  • Square allows eligible sellers to accept bitcoin and receive dollars.

Draper Predicts a Shift From Dollars to Bitcoin

Individuals and companies holding traditional currencies risk falling behind if commerce shifts toward bitcoin, venture capitalist Tim Draper argued on Oct. 28. His warning about bitcoin ownership on X described businesses initially accepting the cryptocurrency alongside other payment methods, then accepting it exclusively.

The founder and managing partner of venture capital firm Draper Associates stated:

“I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again. It’s irresponsible to not own bitcoin.”

That change in merchant preferences would weaken demand for dollars and other government-issued currencies, prompting withdrawals from banks, he predicted. Draper wrote:

“Then people will not value dollars or fiat, and there will be a run on the banks. Eventually, the world will never be the same.”

The warning echoed comments Draper had made in the past about bitcoin ownership and financial preparedness. At the Bitcoin 2026 conference in Las Vegas, he called it irresponsible for companies not to maintain a 5% to 15% bitcoin treasury allocation.

A $250,000 Forecast and Earlier Calls to Hold Bitcoin Reserves

The $250,000 bitcoin target dates to April 2018, when Draper predicted it would be reached by 2022. He subsequently extended the deadline to mid-2023 and later suggested 2025. Those deadlines passed without the target being reached. On April 14, he renewed the forecast with an 18-month window, implying October 2027.

In his Sept. 10 remarks, Draper urged families to hold six months of expenses in bitcoin, companies to cover four weeks of payroll, and governments to allocate part of their treasuries to the cryptocurrency.

Corporate preparedness also featured in his cash management recommendations following Silicon Valley Bank’s collapse in 2023. He advised startups to maintain at least two payrolls’ worth of cash in bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies, alongside six months of short-term cash in each of two banks. Those recommendations addressed access to operating funds during banking disruptions.

Bitcoin Payments Expand Across Platforms and Restaurants

Existing payment infrastructure supports bitcoin transactions while allowing merchants to retain dollar pricing and receipts. Under Square’s bitcoin payment terms, eligible U.S. sellers outside New York can receive bitcoin or choose immediate conversion into dollars. Accepting the cryptocurrency therefore can coexist with continued use of conventional money. Square began its bitcoin payment rollout on Nov. 10, 2025, using the Lightning Network. Other providers also support cryptocurrency checkout, extending payment options across online and physical commerce.

Paypal (Nasdaq: PYPL) offers bitcoin payments with automatic currency conversion through its Pay with Crypto service for eligible U.S. merchants. Customers can pay using bitcoin and other supported cryptocurrencies, while businesses receive funds in their local currency without retaining the digital assets.

Restaurant adoption provides another example: Steak ‘n Shake began accepting bitcoin across its U.S. locations on May 16, 2025, through payment infrastructure provider Speed. Its rollout added bitcoin alongside cash and cards, illustrating the initial acceptance stage Draper described.

Draper outlined the anticipated consequences for bitcoin holders:

“The individuals and companies that are ready for the seismic shift will come out ahead. Those that are left holding legacy currency will not.”

title: Google Cloud Previews Institutional Crypto Key-Security Service as Custody Risks Grow
summary: Google Cloud has documented a Multi-party Compute service for institutional digital-asset custody, describing threshold signing, transaction policy.
content:
TL;DR: Google Cloud has documented a Multi-party Compute service for institutional digital-asset custody, describing threshold signing, transaction policy enforcement and enterprise governance. The market relevance is indirect.

Google Cloud has documented a Multi-party Compute service for institutional digital-asset custody, describing threshold signing, transaction policy enforcement and enterprise governance. The product is in a pre-general-availability stage, with documentation referencing its October 2026 API and migration path. The approach divides signing authority among independent participants so an entire private key does not need to exist in one operational location. This addresses one familiar custody risk, but it does not make cryptocurrency transfers reversible or remove the need to protect approvals and access credentials.

The event and the market response

The company’s technical overview describes a hardened threshold-signing approach and the use of isolated key shares backed by separate hardware environments. A transaction can be authorized when the required participants cooperate, while compromising fewer than the threshold should not give an attacker signing control. Policy checks and enterprise governance allow organizations to set rules around who can request an operation. Google lists secp256k1 signing for Bitcoin and Ethereum-style networks, and its documentation marks Ed25519 support for Solana as coming soon. Availability and blockchain coverage should not be overstated.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

The market relevance is indirect. Stronger institutional custody tools may lower a hurdle for firms considering digital assets, but a preview launch does not create automatic demand for Bitcoin, Ether or any specific token. The more meaningful effect would be regulated institutions becoming comfortable enough with key management to hold and move assets in production. Investors should not assume a major technology company’s entry proves that security risks are solved. It shows that securing private keys remains commercially important as onchain finance expands.

The strongest security response usually looks operational rather than spectacular: inventory exposed systems, restrict unnecessary access, apply verified patches, monitor unusual activity and explain the incident accurately to affected users. Claims of an exploit should not be made when only a possible vulnerability has been identified. At the same time, the absence of a confirmed theft does not eliminate the need for remediation. Trust comes from a provider’s ability to document its response and maintain reliable controls across the third parties and components on which its service depends.

Regulated institutions assessing digital assets must plan for both malicious transactions and ordinary operational failure. A secure key may be unusable after a hardware problem; a correctly signed payment can still reach the wrong destination; a trusted software component may later be compromised. Defense therefore combines cryptography with governance, recovery, vendor oversight and clear human approval. A new security tool or partnership can improve one part of that system without becoming a universal solution. Asking exactly which threats are addressed is more useful than declaring the technology safe or unsafe.

What the headline does not establish

The service aims to address three custody concerns: theft or unauthorized use of a key, temporary inability to sign, and permanent loss of key material. Splitting keys can reduce reliance on a single piece of infrastructure, but it also creates operational questions about participant uptime, recovery, rule administration and who may change policies. Google’s offering remains a technology that banks and other custodians must configure and assess. Independent testing, change management and incident response will be decisive in judging its real-world security value.

What to watch next

The milestones to watch are general availability, demonstrated integrations with regulated custodians and disclosed security evaluations. Practical documentation of recovery and policy administration will be more useful to adopters than a broad claim about eliminating private-key risk.

Primary source: Official statement / source documentation. Additional source: Supporting document 1.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: US Freezes $1 Billion in Crypto as Scam Networks Spread Worldwide
summary: U.S. authorities have restrained more than $1 billion in cryptocurrency as overseas scam networks expand beyond Southeast Asia. New charges describe an alleged Madagascar dating scam that lured Americans into connecting crypto wallets to fraudulent investment websites. Crypto Restraints Cross $1 Bil...
content:
U.S. authorities have restrained more than $1 billion in cryptocurrency as overseas scam networks expand beyond Southeast Asia. New charges describe an alleged Madagascar dating scam that lured Americans into connecting crypto wallets to fraudulent investment websites.

Key Takeaways

  • Investigators identified about 800 U.S. victims of an alleged dating scam.
  • Authorities seized 700 fraudulent cryptocurrency investment websites.
  • Pirro sought extradition of six defendants in the Madagascar case.

Crypto Restraints Cross $1 Billion as Crackdown Expands

More than $1 billion in cryptocurrency tied to fraud and scams was restrained, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia said Oct. 27. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force expanded its global reach as Chinese-linked criminal networks spread into Africa and Europe.

Pirro stated:

“For the last year, the Strike Force has fought hard against the compounds in Southeast Asia facilitating these scammers, to the tune of $1 billion in cryptocurrency restrained.”

She added: “My Strike Force will expand and grow, and follow the scammers to Africa, India, Europe, and wherever they try to plant their operations.”

Launched in November 2025, the strike force had reported more than $580 million in crypto freezes, seizures, and forfeitures within its first three months. Other actions included the seizure of 700 fraudulent investment websites and Telegram channels supporting the schemes.

A September operation against Xinbi Guarantee, a marketplace allegedly serving scam operators, raised cumulative crypto restraints to approximately $938 million. Restraints restrict the use or transfer of assets pending legal proceedings and potential victim compensation.

Across the broader crackdown, private-sector efforts included Meta’s reported removal of 17.3 million scam accounts, OpenAI’s cooperation commitment, and research for a planned consumer-awareness campaign.

Alleged Dating Scam Targeted About 800 Americans

Six defendants were charged over an alleged Madagascar scheme involving fake non-fungible token investments. Participants allegedly posed as women seeking relationships and used fraudulent investment websites to persuade Americans to connect and fund their cryptocurrency wallets before secretly draining them.

Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) investigators identified approximately 74 wallets associated with about 800 U.S. victims. Stolen funds allegedly reached cryptocurrency accounts linked to China-based actors. The group had connections to Malaysia and China and allegedly opened the compounds in Madagascar in early 2025.

Chui Kok Wa, identified by prosecutors as the alleged scheme’s leader, was charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. His phones contained employment contracts with overnight work schedules aligned with U.S. hours and bonuses tied to stolen funds.

US Pursues Suspects as Scam Networks Cross Borders

The United States and Britain signed an agreement Sept. 3 providing for parallel investigations and information sharing against scam networks. Partners included the Crown Prosecution Service, which prosecutes criminal cases in England and Wales, and the National Crime Agency, Britain’s lead agency against serious and organized crime.

Separately, Zheng Zhao’s extradition from the Netherlands brought him before a California court Oct. 23. That case involved 174 identified U.S. victims of an alleged Cambodian investment scheme and falls under the Justice Department’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative.

In Madagascar, an August FBI deployment supported local police targeting 13 compounds, where more than 3,200 electronic devices were seized. U.S. officials described obstacles to interviews and suspects’ repatriation to China before the investigation concluded. Pirro called for the six defendants’ extradition.

The Justice Department described the strike force’s scope:

“The Strike Force targets cryptocurrency investment fraud, cyber-enabled fraud, human trafficking, and money laundering operations that have cost American victims billions of dollars.”

Authorities also obtained a material witness warrant seeking interviews with 15 employees who accused Wa of trafficking and abusing them. Such warrants authorize arrest to secure important testimony when obtaining a witness’s attendance through a subpoena may be impracticable. The Justice Department reported that those employees were believed to remain jailed in Madagascar.

title: Robinhood Crypto Revenue Falls 55% as Prediction Markets Support Growth
summary: Robinhood reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 27, with total net revenue of about $1.42 billion, up 12% from the comparable period a year.
content:
TL;DR: Robinhood reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 27, with total net revenue of about $1.42 billion, up 12% from the comparable period a year earlier. Market participants can learn something from the gap between token narratives and exchange revenue.

Robinhood reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 27, with total net revenue of about $1.42 billion, up 12% from the comparable period a year earlier. Within that record quarter, cryptocurrency transaction revenue fell 55% year over year to $120 million. The company said crypto notional volumes declined 38% to $50 billion across its app and Bitstamp business. Those figures matter because they reveal the difference between the performance of one retail brokerage and the broader idea that digital assets are enjoying continuous commercial growth.

The event and the market response

Robinhood’s other business lines moved in different directions. Options and equities transaction revenue increased, and event contracts contributed $173 million of revenue, more than six times the year-earlier level. The company reported 28.7 million funded customers and 5.2 million Gold subscribers, while platform assets reached about $396 billion. The numbers show a diversifying financial platform in which crypto is an important service but not the only driver of growth. They also remind readers that brokerage revenue depends on activity and pricing, not just the absolute price of the underlying assets.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

Market participants can learn something from the gap between token narratives and exchange revenue. Even if infrastructure projects announce new institutional integrations, retail trading commissions may contract when speculative turnover slows. Robinhood’s results provide a concrete measure of that pressure. They also suggest traders and investors increasingly have other ways to express macro views on the same application. The story is less about a particular token and more about the changing economics of a brokerage exposed to multiple kinds of market activity.

Price-sensitive crypto coverage benefits from keeping three clocks separate: the moment a public announcement was made, the window in which markets reacted and the longer period over which a thesis might be tested. A policy decision or company earnings report can reset expectations immediately, but its enduring effect depends on follow-up data and positioning. Market participants should be wary of treating one narrative as the sole cause of volatile moves. A disciplined reading makes clear what was observed, what was officially disclosed and what remains interpretation.

The connection between digital assets and traditional finance is now too substantial for investors to ignore. Dollar financing rates, the appetite for technology shares, brokerage activity and institutional allocation decisions can all influence crypto demand. None of those relationships is fixed, however: correlation changes as investors rotate between risk and cash. Using a single session to support a dramatic long-term prediction is tempting but unreliable. Readers are better served by a sober distinction between published facts, market observations and forecasts that depend on uncertain assumptions.

What the headline does not establish

A one-quarter performance snapshot should not be mistaken for a definitive verdict on cryptocurrency adoption. Lower notional volume can reflect reduced market volatility, user preferences or changes in trading conditions. Robinhood’s reported Bitstamp and app activity also carry different customer mixes. The quarter does not reveal every possible onchain use case, nor should strong prediction-market performance automatically be attributed to crypto trading. Investors should compare the company’s segment figures over several periods and consider cost, customer assets and the sustainability of newer businesses.

What to watch next

The next earnings report should show whether crypto volume recovers and whether event contracts continue to contribute strongly. Analysts should also monitor trading activity and customer asset trends rather than projecting a long-term outcome from one quarter alone.

Primary source: Official statement / source documentation.

written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Inside the $5.8B Binance Hack: What’s Confirmed and What Isn’t
summary: A suspected security breach at Binance has grown into a multibillion-dollar cryptocurrency emergency, with analysts tracking as much as $5.8 billion in potentially compromised assets across several blockchains. The exchange has suspended withdrawals while Tether, Circle, and other issuers have repor...
content:
A suspected security breach at Binance has grown into a multibillion-dollar cryptocurrency emergency, with analysts tracking as much as $5.8 billion in potentially compromised assets across several blockchains. The exchange has suspended withdrawals while Tether, Circle, and other issuers have reportedly frozen more than $2 billion in tokens. Binance insists customer funds are safe, but investigators are examining how a sophisticated wallet-delegation maneuver may have enabled one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts ever recorded.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance suspended withdrawals Oct. 29 as analysts tracked up to $5.8 billion in suspicious transfers.
  • Tether and Circle reported freezing more than $2.3 billion in tokens linked to the Binance incident.
  • Binance has yet to confirm the final losses or when withdrawals will resume following the Oct. 29 incident.

The trouble began with a few lines of code and a wallet holding an extraordinary amount of money. On Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, cryptocurrency began pouring out of Binance-linked addresses, with one Ethereum transaction reportedly sweeping away roughly 167,464 ETH, 1.615 billion USDT and dozens of other tokens. Within 40 minutes, one receiving address had collected an estimated $3.52 billion.

Then the story took another turn. Analysts identified additional movements involving Bitcoin, Tron and other networks, pushing some estimates beyond $5.5 billion. Stablecoin companies raced to freeze the proceeds, Binance stopped withdrawals, and founder Changpeng Zhao acknowledged that the activity looked like a hack. The exchange itself has yet to confirm a completed theft or its financial toll.

Binance’s Wallet Mystery Grows Into a Multibillion-Dollar Emergency

The first major Ethereum movements began around 4:24 p.m. Eastern time, when assets from a wallet identified as Binance 14 landed in a newly created address. The transfer included more than 60 different tokens, and subsequent transactions brought additional funds from other Binance-linked wallets. Observers and blockchain researchers quickly raised the alarm. By early evening, estimates were climbing as investigators followed assets through different addresses and networks.

The figures were anything but tidy. Some onchain tallies placed the suspected outflows at $5.57 billion across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron. Glassnode estimated roughly $5.3 billion, while broader assessments approached $5.8 billion. Those numbers are preliminary, and some analysts have cautioned that larger estimates may include transfers unrelated to the suspected attack. Binance has not published an independently verified loss figure.

Still, the Ethereum transactions alone were enough to put the industry on notice. For comparison, the February 2025 Bybit hack involved approximately $1.5 billion. Even the narrower Ethereum estimates would exceed that amount.

How a Wallet’s Own Signature May Have Opened the Door

The leading technical explanation centers on EIP-7702, an Ethereum feature introduced with the Pectra upgrade in May 2025. The feature allows an ordinary cryptocurrency wallet to authorize a smart contract to execute instructions on its behalf. It’s useful technology, but that authority becomes dangerous when it ends up in the wrong hands.

Investigators examining Binance 14 identified a delegation transaction submitted at approximately 4:20 p.m. Eastern time. According to Blockaid’s analysis, the transaction contained 50 authorizations designed to account for different possible transaction counters, known as nonces. One matched.

About three minutes later, the wallet’s assets were swept into an external address. Researchers also identified a contract deployed earlier that day and an associated address funded through the ETH mixer Tornado Cash, a cryptocurrency privacy protocol.

The important distinction is that EIP-7702 requires valid authorization. Analysts are examining whether the attacker obtained a private key, tricked an authorized signer into approving malicious instructions or compromised another part of Binance’s signing infrastructure. None of those explanations has been established.

Nor does the Ethereum mechanism explain the reported movements on Bitcoin and Tron. That leaves investigators with a considerably bigger puzzle than a single compromised smart contract.

Ido Ben-Natan, Co-Founder and CEO of Blockaid told Bitcoin.com News that it saw this coming. The firm’s H1 report predicted that a seven-figure exploit would occur in the second half of 2026. “The attacker effectively reprogrammed a major Binance Ethereum hot wallet so that a single operator could drain it, including any new money deposited into it, and they used that access again more than an hour later,” Blockaid’s CEO explained.

Ben-Natan added:

“The attack was planned well in advance, with the attacker funding the operation through Tornado Cash and rehearsing the same takeover on test wallets hours before, all of it visible on-chain. Tether and Circle moved quickly to freeze roughly $2.4 billion, and we are continuing to trace the rest.”

Stablecoin Issuers Drop the Hammer on Billions in Tokens

While investigators worked through the transaction history, stablecoin issuers began cutting off access to assets linked to the suspected exploit. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino reported freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire also confirmed that his company had frozen more than 800 million USDC in coordination with law enforcement.

Binance co-CEO Yi He subsequently credited Ripple with freezing approximately $200 million, while World Liberty Financial co-founder Zach Witkoff reported a separate freeze involving about $27 million in USD1. Taken together, those reported actions represent approximately $2.6 billion, although the figures have not been independently reconciled and should not be treated as a confirmed recovery total.

There’s another catch. Freezing a token isn’t the same as returning it to its rightful owner. Centralized stablecoin issuers can block transfers from designated addresses. Native assets such as bitcoin (BTC) and ether don’t have an equivalent issuer-controlled freeze mechanism. Meanwhile, analysts observed the suspected operator moving ether between wallets, swapping tokens through decentralized trading infrastructure and borrowing against cryptocurrency collateral.

Aave temporarily froze its Ethereum V3 lending markets as a precaution, while maintaining that its smart contracts were unaffected. The result was a race between investigators trying to identify the proceeds and whoever controlled the receiving wallets attempting to move them. Alongside this, the Arbitrum Security Council has executed an onchain transaction to freeze approximately $30.5 million in assets linked to the suspected Binance exploit.

Binance Halts Withdrawals as Zhao Promises Customers Will Be Covered

Binance’s official response remained cautious even as its founder adopted considerably stronger language. The exchange acknowledged a potential security issue and said its teams were investigating. Later Thursday, it suspended withdrawals while conducting security checks, promising to restore access once the issue was resolved. Binance also maintained that customer funds were completely safe.

Zhao, who stepped down as CEO in 2023, offered a more pointed assessment. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” he wrote on X, while emphasizing that he no longer manages the exchange. As a shareholder, he said he expected all customer funds to be covered. In a subsequent post, Zhao suggested the loss might be higher than initially reported and indicated Binance would cover it.

That promise puts the exchange’s financial resources squarely in the spotlight.

“User funds are safe,” Binance’s co-founder and chief customer service officer Yi He wrote at 8 p.m. Eastern time. “Binance will cover all hacking losses. Deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement. We will share a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete. Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates,” the co-founder added.

Crypto Markets Take a Hit as Investigators Face Unanswered Questions

The suspected incident arrived during an already difficult trading session.

Bitcoin fell toward $76,000 before recovering somewhat, while ethereum declined approximately 4.6% and BNB lost nearly 7.7%. Coinglass data shows roughly $1.4 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated within 24 hours, predominantly bullish bets. Not every dollar of those losses can be attributed to Binance. Bitcoin was already under pressure before the suspicious transactions began.

The industry nevertheless found itself in a bind. The largest cryptocurrency exchange by reported platform assets was investigating a potential multibillion-dollar breach, customers temporarily couldn’t withdraw, and security researchers were still piecing together what happened. Questions about the attacker’s identity also remained unanswered. Some researchers raised the possibility of North Korean involvement, but no official attribution had been established.

For now, investigators must determine which transfers were unauthorized, how the necessary wallet permissions were obtained and whether the assets still circulating through external addresses can be recovered. Binance must answer another question: When withdrawals resume, will customers discover that the exchange’s assurances were on the money?

The answer matters far beyond Binance. A company can promise to cover a loss, and token issuers can freeze billions, but neither measure explains how so much cryptocurrency apparently escaped in the first place.

title: Binance points to engineer’s hacked laptop in $6.3B breach
summary: Binance says attackers may have used a compromised DevOps laptop to access internal infrastructure.
content:
Update (Oct. 30 at 2:44 am UTC): This article has been updated to include Binance’s preliminary investigation into the security breach.

Binance said its initial investigation into the multi-billion crypto breach has pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. 

The exchange said the laptop compromise may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. It said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak, though its investigation remains ongoing.

Speaking to Cointelegraph earlier on Thursday, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment also pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key

“It seems to be … a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.

Ben-Natan’s assessment drew on Blockaid’s experience with similar attacks and its observations of the onchain activity.

Binance estimates $6.3 billion impact, freezes about $3 billion

Binance has now put the estimated total impact at around $6.3 billion and said it had worked with blockchain partners to freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets onchain.

The exchange said it would cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, adding that user funds were safe. It also pledged to publish an updated Proof of Reserves.

Binance temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks and said it had revoked the affected address authorization. It is working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds.

The exchange said it would publish a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation was complete and the facts fully verified.

Blockaid identifies malicious wallet delegation

In its onchain analysis published on X, Blockaid said the attacker bundled 50 EIP-7702 authorizations into a single transaction targeting Binance 14. One authorization reportedly matched the account’s required nonce, allowing it to be accepted.

EIP-7702 allows an account to delegate execution to smart-contract code. Blockaid said the affected account was delegated to an unverified sweeper contract that allowed a designated operator to drain tokens and Ether.

Related: Binance hack rattles crypto markets as BNB falls 7%, Bitcoin slides

Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph the operation could have involved multiple compromised devices and movement through the exchange’s network.

Before Binance’s latest update, Arkham CEO Miguel Morel told Cointelegraph there was insufficient information to determine whether the attack involved stolen keys or compromised infrastructure.

“From what we can tell, it appears the hack is still ongoing,” he said at the time.

North Korea, Bybit comparison

Asked whether the suspected signing manipulation resembled the February 2025 Bybit attack, Ben-Natan described the incidents as “very, very similar.”

In that case, Bybit’s published forensic update said attackers compromised a Safe developer’s credentials, accessed the wallet provider’s infrastructure and deceived signers into approving a malicious transaction.

Ben-Natan also said the activity resembled operations linked to North Korea, citing Blockaid’s familiarity with those attacks. He pointed to sophisticated onchain preparations but emphasized that the attribution remained unconfirmed.

Binance has not identified the attackers, saying it is working with law enforcement to establish their identities.

title: Circle and ACI Bring USDC Settlement Into Latin American Payment Operations
summary: ACI Worldwide and Circle announced a collaboration on October 27 to demonstrate how USDC settlement can fit into payment systems that banks already.
content:
TL;DR: ACI Worldwide and Circle announced a collaboration on October 27 to demonstrate how USDC settlement can fit into payment systems that banks already operate. The announcement reinforces an important shift in the stablecoin story: issuance alone is insufficient if enterprises cannot access tokens from the software they already use.

ACI Worldwide and Circle announced a collaboration on October 27 to demonstrate how USDC settlement can fit into payment systems that banks already operate. Their pilot in Colombia uses ACI Connetic, the payments company’s cloud-native orchestration platform, alongside Circle’s infrastructure. The emphasis is on connecting a dollar stablecoin with established account-to-account and institutional payment processes. The parties described a demonstration and collaboration, not a continent-wide production rollout or a guarantee that all transactions will shift to USDC.

The event and the market response

Payments orchestration software connects instructions, processing routes and settlement services. Adding a stablecoin as one settlement option could help institutions evaluate faster cross-border movement or extended operating hours without replacing every other part of their banking stack. ACI positions Connetic as a platform that can accommodate cards, traditional bank payments and digital assets in one environment. Circle supplies infrastructure for USDC, which aims to maintain a dollar value. The experiment therefore focuses as much on operational integration as on the blockchain transfer itself.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

The announcement reinforces an important shift in the stablecoin story: issuance alone is insufficient if enterprises cannot access tokens from the software they already use. ACI’s platform may help USDC move from crypto venues into bank payment operations, but that depends on institutions adopting the workflows and on recipients receiving usable funds. For markets, this is a gradual infrastructure development, not a direct forecast for any cryptocurrency. Track actual corridor usage rather than extrapolating from the size of Latin America’s payments industry.

Settlement networks have different strengths, from established bank accounts to cards and digital tokens. A multi-rail approach can be sensible if software chooses the appropriate method for each obligation while preserving controls and consistent reporting. But offering more rails also adds complexity to pricing, liquidity and risk management. Business customers will not adopt a new option merely because it is technically interesting. They need dependable cost, transparent foreign-exchange treatment and accurate delivery times. That is the benchmark for judging payments announcements.

A cross-border payment has at least two meanings of speed: how quickly value moves between institutions, and how quickly the recipient can spend it. Stablecoin settlement can improve the first without necessarily solving the second. Real-world payouts require local networks, liquidity, compliance screening and customer support. The strongest payment partnerships join those pieces rather than attempting to replace everything with one blockchain. Readers should look for end-to-end performance data and distinguish existing network size from transaction volume that actually uses a newly announced digital rail.

What the headline does not establish

A successful pilot must still confront local regulation, the treatment of dollar balances, liquidity provision and how financial institutions reconcile stablecoin settlement with their books. An onchain transfer that completes quickly is only one stage of a bank payment. Currency conversion, compliance checks, beneficiary access and final accounting can still introduce delay or cost. ACI and Circle have not presented comprehensive live-market data proving savings across Latin America. The confirmed development is a practical test of whether old and new rails can work together.

What to watch next

Look for pilot performance results, additional bank participants and clarity about which payment corridors move into production. A real-world expansion should be measured by settled transaction value and operational outcomes, not announcement count.

title: Onchain Lending Fees Plunge 50% as Morpho Bucks the Trend
summary: According to a report by 1kx, onchain lending markets contracted significantly in 2026, with user-paid fees dropping approximately 50% year over year. New Market Trading CEO Frank Hepworth cautions against locking up bitcoin for low fixed yields, citing high smart contract and counterparty risks. Ke...
content:
According to a report by 1kx, onchain lending markets contracted significantly in 2026, with user-paid fees dropping approximately 50% year over year. New Market Trading CEO Frank Hepworth cautions against locking up bitcoin for low fixed yields, citing high smart contract and counterparty risks.

Key Takeaways

  • Onchain lending fees plunged 50% year-over-year in 2026 following a Q2 KelpDAO exploit, per 1kx data.
  • Aave lost deposits, but Morpho expanded, earning $62M in Q3 2026 via curator risk managers.
  • Platforms are targeting tokenized Treasuries like PYUSD to offer institutions safer 1–4% yields.

KelpDAO Exploit Impact on Market Leaders

Onchain lending markets experienced a sharp contraction in 2026, with user-paid fees falling approximately 50% year over year, according to a new report from crypto investment firm 1kx. However, despite the broader downturn, decentralized lending protocol Morpho demonstrated resilience, recording a modest increase in fees during the third quarter.

According to the 2026 1kx Blockchain Revenue Report, lending markets remained relatively stable during the first half of the year before deteriorating significantly in the third quarter, when fees declined 46% compared with the same period in 2025.

The report attributes much of the sector’s weakness to Aave, the leading decentralized lending protocol, which suffered a significant decline in deposits following the KelpDAO exploit in the second quarter of 2026. Although Aave subsequently began recovering lost deposits, the report describes the recovery as gradual, suggesting that the impact of the exploit continued to weigh on the protocol’s performance.

The lending sector’s contraction occurred against a broader decline in blockchain industry revenues. According to 1kx, total blockchain revenues are projected to reach approximately $100 billion in 2026, down 30% from the roughly $140 billion generated in 2025. The decline broadly mirrors the decrease in bitcoin’s average price over the same period.

Despite the downturn, decentralized finance (DeFi) and other financial applications remained the industry’s largest revenue-generating category, accounting for approximately $65 billion, or 66% of projected blockchain revenues.

While Aave struggled with declining deposits, Morpho emerged as one of the sector’s more resilient platforms. The protocol, which ranked second among lending markets by fees, generated $62 million in user-paid fees during the third quarter of 2026, representing a slight increase despite the broader market contraction.

The report attributes Morpho’s relative strength to its curator-based lending model, under which specialized risk managers oversee individual lending markets. According to 1kx, much of the fees generated through Morpho’s lending markets accrued to risk curators such as Steakhouse and Gauntlet rather than directly to the protocol.

The contrasting performances of Aave and Morpho illustrate how differences in lending market structures and risk management can influence revenue generation during periods of reduced market activity. Morpho’s performance also helped secure its position among the 20 leading blockchain protocols by user-paid fees in 2026, according to the report.

Institutional Yield Strategies Face Risk and Return Trade-Offs

The downturn in lending market revenues has also brought renewed attention to how investors can generate predictable returns without assuming excessive exposure to cryptocurrency price volatility.

Frank Hepworth, CEO and founder of New Market Trading, said institutions seeking relatively stable yields during prolonged market consolidation should prioritize less volatile assets rather than rely heavily on cryptocurrency-backed lending.

According to Hepworth, stablecoins deployed across actively managed DeFi yield vaults can provide one approach, although investors must account for the additional risks introduced by third-party platforms and strategies. He also pointed to tokenized government Treasuries and private credit arrangements, including those offered by Maple Finance, as alternatives that institutions are increasingly adopting onchain.

Hepworth cautioned that the economics of lending bitcoin are less compelling, particularly when compared with other strategies available during strong market rallies.

“Locking up BTC is almost always a poor risk-reward. Real BTC demand to borrow is thin, so the 1 to 4% on offer mostly comes from token emissions, while you take on derivative, counterparty and smart contract risk to earn it,” Hepworth said.

He argued that the opportunity cost becomes particularly pronounced during bull markets, when the annualized premium on CME bitcoin futures can rise well above the returns available through fixed-rate lending products.

“In bull runs it gets worse: CME basis often runs well into the teens, so whoever holds your BTC can earn far more on it than they pay you. You carry their risk for a fraction of the spread,” he added.

His assessment highlights a potential challenge for bitcoin holders seeking yield: Fixed lending returns may fail to compensate investors adequately for the risks assumed or the upside opportunities forgone. Hepworth identified several strategies that could still allow investors to generate returns, including providing liquidity to closely correlated bitcoin-backed assets, such as cbBTC and WBTC. He also suggested borrowing stablecoins against bitcoin collateral and deploying the borrowed funds into higher-yielding opportunities.

Still, Hepworth warned that liquidity pools involving wrapped bitcoin expose investors to risks associated with the underlying tokens, while leveraged stablecoin strategies can become vulnerable when borrowing costs rise or collateral values decline. He also highlighted covered-call strategies, which involve selling options against bitcoin holdings to collect premiums, as an increasingly popular approach.

“It looks attractive when IV is high to earn yield on your BTC, but the premium is high for a reason: The market is pricing big moves,” he said.

He warned that investors employing covered calls during aggressive rallies risk having their bitcoin sold at the option’s strike price, potentially forfeiting further upside. For institutions seeking more predictable returns, Hepworth suggested that structured credit products combining a contractual base return with performance-linked profit sharing could provide a more balanced approach.

“The best structure would be a contractual base return for predictable institutional income, with a hurdle-gated profit-share on top so investors only share in outperformance once that base is delivered,” he explained.

Tokenized Assets Emerge as New Lending Market Opportunity

Despite declining onchain lending activity, 1kx identifies tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) as an emerging battleground for Aave and Morpho, particularly tokenized U.S. Treasuries and private credit.

The report highlights a Sentora-curated Morpho vault offering PYUSD loans against Figure’s PRIME home-equity token, alongside GPU-backed lending through USD.ai.

These developments support Hepworth’s view that institutions may increasingly favor stablecoins, tokenized government debt and structured credit over low-yielding bitcoin lending. However, such products still carry counterparty, liquidity and smart contract risks.

With lending fees down approximately 50% year over year, Morpho’s resilience and growing demand for tokenized collateral suggest a shift toward specialized credit markets. Their long-term appeal will depend on whether returns adequately compensate institutions for the risks involved.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Posts Record Operating Income as Bitcoin Rebounds in Q3 2026
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Posts Record Operating Income as Bitcoin Rebounds in Q3 2026
Strategy reported record $20.91 billion in Q3 2026 operating income, driven by Bitcoin’s rebound, despite declining revenue, negative year-to-date BTC yield, and continued pressure to fund preferred divide...
content:
Strategy posted the largest operating income in its history on Thursday, booking $20.91 billion for the third quarter of 2026. Most of that total came from a paper gain on the company’s bitcoin stack. 

Net income reached $19.53 billion, or $44.75 per diluted share, up from $2.79 billion a year earlier. 

Chief Financial Officer Andrew Kang, who announced his departure in the same release, framed the result plainly: “Q3 operating income of $21 billion was the largest ever in Strategy’s history.”

Strategy marks its bitcoin to market each quarter, so every price move flows into earnings. Bitcoin rallied during the period. The company’s 848,517 bitcoin were worth $68.9 billion as of October 23, when the token traded at $81,200. The holdings carry an average cost of $75,446, which leaves the position in the black on paper. 

Kang pointed to the purchases as the engine of the quarter, saying the company “increased our bitcoin holdings by 26% year-to-date in a challenging bitcoin market.”

Total revenue fell 3%from a year ago to $125.4 million, below analyst estimates of $127.2 million. Gross profit came in at $89.6 million, a 71% margin compared with 70% a year earlier. The company ended September with $2.50 billion in cash and equivalents and $3.40 billion in short-term investments.

Strategy’s bitcoin per share slips

Bitcoin per share, the metric management uses as its main yardstick, moved the other way. The BTC yield stands at negative 3.7% for the year, meaning each share holds less bitcoin than it did in January. Measured in dollars, the bitcoin position shows a $2.03 billion loss over the same period. To fund preferred dividends and stock buybacks, the company has sold roughly $431.8 million of bitcoin this year, a figure the release puts at approximately that amount.

Strategy raised $21.23 billion of capital in 2026, including $5.41 billion in net proceeds from its at-the-market program during the third quarter alone. The company then spent a large part of that money on its own preferred stock. It repurchased 20,980,508 shares of STRC for $2.04 billion at an average of $97.39 per share, a discount to the $100 stated amount.

Chief Executive Phong Le said the buyback program was meant to put the security on firmer footing: “Strategy demonstrated its commitment to returning STRC to health.” Management said it intends to keep buying while STRC trades below par, and about $956.7 million remains under the authorization.

The company’s dollar reserves now total $5.07 billion, made up of a $4.83 billion USD Reserve and $242.4 million of USD Cash. Strategy says that cushion covers 3.4 years of dividend and interest obligations. The board kept the STRC dividend rate at 12.00% to support trading near the $100 stated amount.

STRC moves to daily dividends

Shareholders approved a move to daily dividends on October 28. STRC begins paying daily on November 1, and STRF, STRK, and STRD follow on January 1, 2027. 

Le framed the change as a step toward a different kind of market: “Daily dividends are a natural step toward the tokenized, 24/7/365 financial system. Digital Credit is being built for that world, and Strategy intends to lead it.” 

Strategy also expects its preferred distributions to count as a non-taxable return of capital for ten years or more, because it does not expect positive accumulated earnings and profits. Shareholders should consult their own tax advisers.

That said, Strategy’s STRC stock is nearing $100. Earlier today, STRC reached $99.99 which once par would reopen funding for Bitcoin purchases. As mentioned ealier, shareholders approved daily dividends to improve liquidity and reduce price volatility. That said, Strategy has not yet confirmed a restart of STRC share issuance.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bitcoin Price Slides Below $79,000 as Binance Loses $5.8 Billion in Massive Hack
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slides Below $79,000 as Binance Loses $5.8 Billion in Massive Hack
Bitcoin price fell below $79,000 as reports of a suspected Binance hack, with outflows of up to $5.8 billion, prompted Tether and Circle to freeze roughly $1.8 to $2.4 billion in stablecoins.
This post...
content:
Bitcoin dropped below $79,000 on Thursday as reports of a suspected multibillion-dollar hack at Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, rippled through markets. 

The selloff followed reports of heavy outflows from Binance-linked wallets. Some social media reports cited suspicious outflows of up to $5.8 billion, citing onchain data that shows about $3.55 billion in incoming transfers to an unlabeled wallet. 

Conor Grogan, a senior director at Coinbase, put the figure at $5.8 billion.

Stablecoin issuers moved to freeze funds. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze more than 1.567 billion USDT. Circle froze about $823 million in USDC, according to former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao, who remains a shareholder. 

Combined freezes range from $1.8 billion to $2.4 billion depending on reports. “Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority,” Ardoino said.

Binance has made no official confirmation of a breach. Co-founder Yi He wrote on X that the company is aware of reports of a potential security issue and that its security teams are reviewing all relevant information. 

“We are aware of reports of a potential security issue and we are actively investigating…our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information. Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”

Zhao wrote that, in his view, the exchange appears to have been hacked, and he expects all user funds to be covered.

“I don’t manage Binance anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered,” Zhao posted.

Blockchain researcher Spreek flagged the activity, which reportedly included a transfer through a contract call allegedly funded by Tornado Cash. Blockaid said it is investigating $3.3 billion in suspicious outflows from Binance hot wallets across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche.

If confirmed, the incident would be the largest crypto theft on record, surpassing the February 2025 Bybit hack of roughly $1.5 billion. Aave reportedly froze lending markets to block the suspected attacker from borrowing. 

Binance.US said the incident does not affect its platform.

Figures remain fluid. One estimate puts the realized loss near 0.7% of Binance customer assets, and other reports continue to revise totals. Neither Binance nor law enforcement has released a formal account of the cause.

Crypto exchange Bybit was not affected. They tweeted that their “systems are operating normally, trading and withdrawals remain available, and user assets remain secure.”

Bitcoin price drops under $79,000 after Binance hack jitters

Bitcoin is trading at $78,800, down 2.89% (about $2,350) over the past 24 hours. The price hit a 24-hour high of $81,890 around midday before sliding sharply after 4 p.m. ET, when it fell to a low of $78,177.37, after rumors of the hack circulated. 

Trading volume over the period was about $26.14 billion, and bitcoin’s market cap stands at roughly $1.58 trillion.

title: DBS Survey Finds 88% of Businesses Testing or Using Tokenized Money
summary: A DBS survey published October 28 found that 88% of businesses in its sample were deploying or piloting tokenized-money use cases. Crypto traders sometimes.
content:
TL;DR: A DBS survey published October 28 found that 88% of businesses in its sample were deploying or piloting tokenized-money use cases. Crypto traders sometimes treat institutional survey results as proof that public token demand must surge.

A DBS survey published October 28 found that 88% of businesses in its sample were deploying or piloting tokenized-money use cases. The Singapore bank presented the results as evidence of growing interest in round-the-clock money movement, better liquidity management and expansion across trading corridors. Respondents also reported reworking treasury and finance processes against a backdrop of shifting supply chains. The headline percentage combines testing with deployment; it does not mean that 88% of large companies have replaced their traditional bank accounts with stablecoins.

The event and the market response

The survey connects tokenized money to a set of practical corporate needs. A multinational business may need to move funds among subsidiaries, pay suppliers in different currencies or reconcile balances after local payment systems have closed. Tokenized deposits and stablecoins can be evaluated for particular parts of those tasks, but successful treasury integration requires approvals, liquidity, accounting and reliable conversion to conventional balances. The bank also reported that more than three quarters of respondents expected AI to improve treasury, payment or collection operations over the next two years.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

Crypto traders sometimes treat institutional survey results as proof that public token demand must surge. That conclusion is too quick. Corporations may adopt privately operated payment systems or bank-issued tokenized deposits without taking directional exposure to volatile cryptocurrencies. The stronger market implication is demand for dependable settlement services and stable-value balances. Investors should ask which networks are actually used, how much real value they carry and whether adoption persists beyond early experiments.

An institutional buyer will evaluate the cost of connecting a new rail to its existing systems before celebrating the technology. That includes identity checks, transaction reporting, asset servicing, reconciliation and recovery procedures when something goes wrong. A smaller but repeatable workflow can be commercially more valuable than an enormous theoretical market size. In this case, progress should be measured against the promised operational improvement and the conditions attached to it. Without usage figures, no one can reliably turn a partnership or infrastructure milestone into a forecast of investment returns.

Tokenized finance is often described as a single market, but it covers quite different instruments: cash-like balances, securities, private credit and other claims. Each has different settlement and counterparty risks. Institutional adoption becomes meaningful when service providers can explain who owes what, how a holder exits a position and what happens during a dispute. The detail matters as much as speed. A sound launch can be the beginning of a larger change, although the step from successful integration to widespread, economically useful activity is rarely automatic.

What the headline does not establish

Survey evidence requires attention to definitions and sampling. A pilot can be a limited experiment, while live deployment might serve only a small fraction of a company’s transactions. Firms may also mean different things by tokenized money, including privately issued bank liabilities, stablecoins and representations of deposits. DBS has a commercial role in the financial-services market it is analyzing, making the methodological details especially important. The finding is useful as a measure of reported interest, but less informative than independently verified volumes and operating savings.

What to watch next

The next useful disclosures would break out pilots from production deployments, distinguish stablecoins from tokenized deposits and report measurable savings or settlement volumes. Those would help establish whether strong survey interest is becoming large-scale use.
