title: Strategy’s $21B Quarter Is Its Biggest Ever as Saylor Sees New Bitcoin Bull Run
summary: Strategy reported record operating profit as bitcoin gains lifted quarterly results, while Michael Saylor said a new bull market was beginning. Daily preferred dividends and a CFO transition accompanied the earnings announcement. Bitcoin Gains Lift Operating Profit to a Record Record operating incom...
content:
Strategy reported record operating profit as bitcoin gains lifted quarterly results, while Michael Saylor said a new bull market was beginning. Daily preferred dividends and a CFO transition accompanied the earnings announcement.

Key Takeaways

  • Operating income totaled $20.91 billion; diluted earnings per share were $44.75.
  • Bitcoin holdings reached 848,517 BTC, up 26% year to date.
  • STRC preferred share dividends accrue from Nov. 1; payments begin Nov. 2.

Bitcoin Gains Lift Operating Profit to a Record

Record operating income of $20.91 billion and diluted earnings per share of $44.75 marked Strategy Inc.’s (Nasdaq: MSTR) third-quarter results, announced Oct. 29. The bitcoin treasury and enterprise software company recognized $20.91 billion in digital asset gains, compared with $3.89 billion a year earlier.

Operating income measures profit after operating expenses, before interest and income taxes; Strategy includes bitcoin valuation gains in that figure. Net income totaled $19.53 billion, including $19.12 billion attributable to common stockholders, while revenue declined 3% to $125.4 million.

Chief Financial Officer Andrew Kang stated: “Q3 operating income of $21 billion was the largest ever in Strategy’s history. We’ve also raised $21 billion of equity capital and increased our bitcoin holdings by 26% year-to-date in a challenging bitcoin market.”

Founder and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor offered a bullish outlook:

“We’re at the beginning of the next bitcoin bull market. Banks are embracing bitcoin, bitcoin’s dominance among digital assets is growing, institutional demand is back, and bitcoin price is 21% above its 200-week moving average.”

Treasury Expands as Bitcoin Per Share Falls

The company’s 848,517-bitcoin treasury cost $64.02 billion, averaging $75,446 per coin, as of Oct. 25. Year-to-date bitcoin purchases totaled $14.33 billion. Holdings were valued at $68.90 billion using the Oct. 23 bitcoin price of $81,200.

That position represented approximately 4% of bitcoin’s maximum supply of 21 million coins. MSTR shares rose 76% during the third quarter, compared with bitcoin’s 43% advance.

BTC Yield, which tracks percentage changes in bitcoin per assumed diluted share, was negative 3.7% year to date. This share count includes potential shares from convertible securities and equity awards. Holdings therefore grew more slowly than that share count. BTC Gain expresses that change in bitcoin units using beginning-of-year holdings. Its negative 24,947 BTC result reflected per-share dilution. Neither metric measures investment returns.

Daily Dividends Accompany Finance Leadership Changes

Shareholders approved daily preferred stock dividends on Oct. 28, with accrual for Stretch (STRC), a variable-rate perpetual preferred stock, starting Nov. 1. Strife (STRF), Strike (STRK), and Stride (STRD), fixed-rate perpetual preferreds that currently pay quarterly, follow on Jan. 1, 2027. These preferred shares rank senior to MSTR common stock for dividends but are not collateralized by Strategy’s bitcoin. Dividends will accrue on weekends and holidays, with cash payments potentially combined on business days.

Management maintained STRC’s 12% annual dividend rate to support trading near its $100 stated amount. Dollar assets totaled $5.07 billion, providing an estimated 3.4 years of coverage for preferred dividends and interest obligations.

Capital allocation included no bitcoin purchases and $204.9 million in STRC buybacks during Oct. 19-25. Year-to-date repurchases totaled $2.04 billion, including unsettled transactions. Strategy sold approximately $431.8 million of bitcoin during 2026 to help fund preferred dividends and STRC repurchases.

Kang will step down Nov. 5 and remain an adviser through Dec. 31, while President and CEO Phong Le assumes finance oversight during the transition. Executive Vice President of Operations Reza Virasteh becomes CFO Jan. 1, 2027, serving as co-principal financial officer alongside Le, who retains responsibility for financial management of the bitcoin strategy.

title: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express
summary: Singapore police say tampered Ledgers started showing up there on September 10. South Korean lawmakers look set to delay the crypto tax law for a fourth time.
content:
Tampered Ledger wallets cost Singapore users $2.7M: Police

Singapore police say at least two cases involving tampered Ledger hardware wallets have been reported since Sept. 10, with combined losses of about 3.5 million Singapore dollars ($2.7 million). It places the first local report almost a month before the wider incident became public.

It’s not clear from the October 28 consumer alert if the September 10 case was reported to police at the time, or was made retrospectively. If the report was timely, it raises questions as to whether Ledger was informed, or if the Singapore Police Force was in a position to issue a public warning earlier. However, the October 28 advisory suggested the police investigation was still in the preliminary stages.

Ledger issued a public alert about tampered Ledgers being found in the CryptoBilis supply chain on October 9. Almost $100 million was drained from wallets containing spyware components.

On Oct. 13, Ledger said it has asked retailers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Hong Kong to suspend sales of Ledger devices as investigations are ongoing.

Singapore police issue tampered Ledgers warning three weeks after the story broke. Source: Singapore Police

Malaysia, Thailand join Singapore’s cross-border stablecoin push

Bank Negara Malaysia and the Bank of Thailand joined Singapore’s BLOOM initiative on Friday as policymaker members.

BLOOM, short for Borderless, Liquid, Open, Online, Multi-currency, is a public-private initiative that intends to help financial institutions use stablecoins and tokenized deposits for cross-border payments. It was launched by the Monetary Authority of Singapore in October last year and counts Airwallex, Mastercard, Ripple, Visa and the World Bank Group as members.

DBS survey finds lots of corporate interest in tokenized money

A survey by Singapore bank DBS found that almost 90% of 422 global businesses surveyed are either adopting, or are interested in adopting, tokenized cash to accelerate payments.

SOUTH KOREA

Groundhog Day as Korean lawmakers consider fourth delay of crypto tax

Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing another delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently scheduled to be implemented in January 2027. 

According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.

The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually.

Bithumb and two other firms report data breaches

Bithumb said its in-house mobile system was hacked and personal information leaked. Brokerage Daishin Securities reported roughly 38,000 customer records exposed and asset manager Mirae Asset Global Investments confirmed a hacking incident.

South Korea to regulate stablecoins as payment means, and require monthly balance reporting for cross border transfers

The South Korean government and the Bank of Korea intend to draft amendments to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act within this year to regulate stablecoins used as payment instruments. The central bank will also require crypto transfer service providers to send monthly reports from December 2 — but extending back to mid 2024 — about who exactly has been sending money out of the country.

NORTH KOREA

Chainalysis traces North Korean crypto cash-outs through Garantex

Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis mapped a long-running network of Russian intermediaries that helped North Korean IT workers cash out millions of dollars in cryptocurrency.

The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity on Wednesday for supporting North Korean government-run IT worker schemes that it said funded the country’s weapons programs, according to a press release.

Those sanctioned included Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas. 

HONG KONG

Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise

Hong Kong has named Nasdaq-listed Solana Company (HSDT) a strategic enterprise under a government program aimed at attracting businesses that support the city’s economic development.

Solana Company said Thursday that it was among the seventh batch of businesses selected by Hong Kong’s Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES) and the only blockchain infrastructure company onboarded by the office in 2026.

Hong Kong’s government confirmed the addition of 18 enterprises to the program last week, bringing its total to 142.

China uses Hong Kong as a launchpad for the Digital Yuan

The South China Morning Post reported that Beijing wants Hong Kong to help seed international use of the digital yuan.

RedotPay plans a US IPO

Hong Kong crypto payments firm RedotPay plans to launch an IPO in the US before the end of the year, and has launched a pre-IPO funding round valuing the company at $4 billion.

CHINA

China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout

China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.

The new plan also calls for stronger blockchain technical standards and greater use of the technology in data circulation and trading.

Mainland China bans cryptocurrency-related business activities, but promotes blockchain technology as a national priority. Critics say that blockchain-not-crypto has never worked before.

THAILAND

Supreme Court recognizes Bitcoin as legal property

Thailand’s Supreme Court has ruled that Bitcoin qualifies as property under criminal law, setting a precedent that may influence how Thai courts treat other cryptocurrencies. The case involved upholding a 10-year prison sentence in a robbery case involving about $50,000 in Bitcoin.

Thailand launches crypto wallet for tourists

Thailand has launched the terribly named WORPT digital wallet so that tourists can convert USDT or USDC into Thai baht in order to spend via PromptPay QR codes. The scheme is part of the Tourist DigiPay sandbox.

title: Hedera Ecosystem Adds Bron Self-Custody Platform Through Industry Association
summary: Self-custody platform Bron announced on October 28 that it had joined the Hashgraph Association’s Global Membership Program. The news touches Hedera’s.
content:
TL;DR: Self-custody platform Bron announced on October 28 that it had joined the Hashgraph Association’s Global Membership Program. The news touches Hedera’s growth narrative without providing a direct HBAR demand estimate.

Self-custody platform Bron announced on October 28 that it had joined the Hashgraph Association’s Global Membership Program. Bron already supports the holding and management of HBAR and Hedera-based digital assets, according to the joint announcement, with a swap interface that relies on third-party solvers and smart contracts. Membership is designed to connect Bron more directly with enterprises, developers and other organizations in the Hedera ecosystem. It is not the announcement of a new Hedera protocol, guaranteed wallet protection or an exclusive exchange listing.

The event and the market response

Self-custody places control of assets and signing authority with users or organizations rather than relying entirely on a centralized exchange account. That can remove some counterparty exposure, but it creates distinct responsibilities around key recovery, device security and approving transactions. Bron describes its product as digital wealth infrastructure intended to serve assets that may include tokenized securities and stablecoins as onchain finance develops. The association says its program includes industry collaboration, technical resources and opportunities for ecosystem participants to connect.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

The news touches Hedera’s growth narrative without providing a direct HBAR demand estimate. Better wallet support can reduce friction for people who want to hold or use a network’s assets, but new membership is a step removed from daily active usage. Traders should avoid converting a partner announcement into a token-price forecast. Evidence worth following would include supported financial products, real wallet engagement and whether institutions adopt the platform with documented security procedures.

Cryptocurrency security is not one problem. Private-key protection, account permissions, vendor data access and the trust placed in external infrastructure all create separate paths to loss or disruption. It is possible for a blockchain to function correctly while a wallet, exchange partner or software runtime still exposes users to avoidable risk. Coverage should identify the affected layer and the controls available to limit harm. Broad statements that funds are safe or a patch exists are useful, but informed readers also need to know the limits of those assurances.

The strongest security response usually looks operational rather than spectacular: inventory exposed systems, restrict unnecessary access, apply verified patches, monitor unusual activity and explain the incident accurately to affected users. Claims of an exploit should not be made when only a possible vulnerability has been identified. At the same time, the absence of a confirmed theft does not eliminate the need for remediation. Trust comes from a provider’s ability to document its response and maintain reliable controls across the third parties and components on which its service depends.

What the headline does not establish

The group cites more than 190 corporate members, while Bron’s release places the membership within a wider effort to promote Hedera adoption. Those broad community totals should not be interpreted as Bron’s own customer numbers or new onchain transaction volume. Similarly, supporting an asset in a wallet does not certify the risk of every third-party swap route offered through an interface. Independent security assessments, clear transaction previews and reliable recovery options will matter far more to users than ecosystem affiliation alone.

What to watch next

Watch for specific technical integrations, independent security disclosures and measurable user adoption resulting from the association membership. Those will determine whether the partnership changes the practical experience of holding Hedera assets.

title: Eagles Star Saquon Barkley Says NFL Forced Him to Sell Polymarket Stake
summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said he had to give up his equity stake in Polymarket because NFL rules bar players from investing in prediction markets. The admission comes days after the NBA named the platform alongside Kalshi as preferred prediction market partners.   The NFL Trea...
content:
Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said he had to give up his equity stake in Polymarket because NFL rules bar players from investing in prediction markets. The admission comes days after the NBA named the platform alongside Kalshi as preferred prediction market partners.

Key Takeaways

  • Saquon Barkley told Front Office Sports he sold his Polymarket stake to comply with NFL rules.
  • The NFL bars players from investing in or endorsing prediction markets, which it treats like sportsbooks.

The NFL Treats Prediction Markets Like Sportsbooks

Barkley told Front Office Sports that he had to divest his Polymarket investment after the league made clear that players cannot hold stakes in prediction market companies.

“I am not in that right now,” he said. “I am not allowed to be in that.”

The NFL briefs players before each season on what they can and can’t do with endorsements and investments, Barkley said. Prediction markets fall under a particular ban in that department.

“So I kinda had to get out of that,” he added. “I was in it before, but no bueno.”

Polymarket was among the startup investments revealed in a profile of Barkley last September. Sometime between then and this summer, the league told players they could not have financial interests in prediction market platforms. The NFL confirmed on Wednesday that its ban on investing in and promoting sportsbooks extends to prediction markets, but declined to comment specifically on Barkley’s case. Polymarket also declined to comment.

Neither the size of Barkley’s stake nor when he sold it has been disclosed. An NFL Players Association spokesperson said in January that the league “views prediction markets as gambling entities, so players are not allowed to be an endorser or brand ambassador for a company like Kalshi or Polymarket under the gambling policy.”

Unlike the other major American sports leagues, which have now almost fully come around on partnering with prediction markets, the NFL has kept its distance from the sector.

When it signed DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics as sportsbook partners in August, a league executive said prediction markets were not a space it was considering commercially. The league barred prediction market ads from last year’s Super Bowl. This month it urged the Supreme Court to take up New Jersey’s case against Kalshi, and it has said it believes prediction markets should, for now, be regulated at the state level.

The NBA named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction market partners earlier this week, and reportedly does not stop players from investing in or endorsing them, as long as they don’t promote NBA-related contracts. LeBron James, who teased a Polymarket partnership in September, has a deal with the company that is reportedly worth $15 million a year.

Major League Baseball signed an exclusive Polymarket deal in March, reportedly worth up to $300 million over four years, while the NHL has partnered with both Kalshi and Polymarket. The MLS, like the MLB, has only partnered with Polymarket at the league level.

title: Live updates: Binance says $6.3B hack possibly involved a compromised engineer’s laptop
summary: Follow live updates as Binance says $6.3 billion in assets has been stolen in a major hack, with further freezes possible as investigators trace funds.
content:
What we know about the Binance hack:

  • Binance says the estimated total impact is around $6.3 billion and the verified total value of crypto frozen is $3 billion. This could increase as investigators trace additional assets.
  • Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals and deposits.
  • Assets frozen include Tether USDt (USDT), USDC (USDC), Ripple USD (RLUSD), World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), StraitsX USD (XUSD), USDT0 (USDT0), Wrapped Beacon ETH (WBETH), Tether Gold (XAUT), Pax Gold (PAXG), Pax Dollar (USDP) and Arbitrum (ARB).
  • The incident did not impact Binance.US.

Oct. 30 at 02:25 am UTC

Binance points to engineer’s hacked laptop in $6.3B breach

Binance said its initial investigation into the multi-billion crypto breach has pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. 

The exchange said the laptop compromise may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. It said it had found no evidence of a wallet private-key leak, though its investigation remains ongoing.

The crypto exchange has also disclosed that the estimated total impact of the hack is $6.3 billion. 

Oct. 30 at 02:21 am UTC

First Digital confirms it has frozen FDUSD involved in attack

First Digital CEO Vincent Chok said it has frozen the FDUSD stolen in the attack on Binance. 

“We’re working alongside the Binance team and will share updates as we have them,” Chok told Cointelegraph in a written statement. 

“Our priority is protecting FDUSD holders and stopping bad actors from moving stolen funds. Protecting users is a responsibility we all share.”

Oct. 30 at 01:19 am UTC

Bitcoin trades below $77,000 as BNB falls 8% 

Bitcoin traded near $76,937, down 4.9% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. BNB fell 8% to about $693, while Ether declined 5.7% to about $2,211.

DeFi tokens also fell, with AAVE down 11.3% and Uniswap’s UNI down 10.7% over the same period.

The Bitcoin Fear and Greed Index, which tracks Bitcoin market sentiment, fell to “fear” with a score of 30, which it has not seen since August.

Oct. 30 at 12:52 am UTC

Binance says $3 billion now frozen from hack

Binance said the current verified amount of assets frozen from the hack is now $3 billion.

The update came after the Arbitrum Security Council said it executed a transaction to freeze $30.5 million from the Binance exploit, involving 74.6 million Arbitrum (ARB) and 8,425 Ether (ETH).

“The Security Council acted by weighing its commitment to the security and integrity of the Arbitrum community and Arbitrum governance without impacting any Arbitrum users or applications,” it said.

“As of October 30, 2026 time, the funds have been successfully transferred to an intermediary frozen wallet,” it said.

The funds will no longer be accessible to the address that originally held the funds and can only be moved by further action of the Security Council or a vote of Arbitrum DAO governance, it added.

Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC

Chainalysis estimates $5.9 billion stolen from Binance

Chainalysis said its current estimate of the amount stolen from Binance is $5.912 billion at the time of theft, four times the amount stolen from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.

Binance earlier said the verified total frozen is $2.54 billion.

Oct. 30 at 12:26 am UTC

Blockaid suspects Binance hack involved private key “misuse”

The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.

Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key. 

“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.

Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.

Arkham CEO Miguel Morel said the attack appears to be ongoing.

Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC

Binance says deposits temporarily suspended

Binance said it has temporarily suspended deposits as it conducts security checks, freezes funds and coordinates with law enforcement. It previously confirmed it had suspended withdrawals.

“We are working around the clock and will share a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete,” the company said, adding it will “cover all losses.”

Earlier, Binance also said it had temporarily suspended Binance Alpha trading.

Oct. 30 at 12:07 am UTC

Wintermute and GSR disclose Binance exposure

Crypto trading firms Wintermute and GSR disclosed exposure to Binance but said they did not expect major disruption to their businesses.

The firms are market makers, which place buy and sell orders on exchanges to help other traders complete transactions. A disruption to their operations could make trading harder or more expensive across crypto markets.

GSR CEO Xin Song said its Binance exposure was less than 5% of its net equity, meaning the value of its assets minus its liabilities. He said GSR was working with Binance to understand the incident and identify ways to help.

Wintermute CEO Evgeny Gaevoy said his firm’s exposure was less than 20% of net equity and that he did not expect operational disruption.

Neither executive disclosed a dollar amount for the exposure or confirmed financial losses.

Oct. 29 at 11:40 pm UTC

Ripple freezes RLUSD linked to Binance hack

Ripple is freezing holdings of its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin linked to the Binance hack, according to Jack McDonald, the company’s senior vice president of stablecoins.

McDonald said Ripple was “actively freezing affected funds” and coordinating with relevant parties to support the investigation. He did not disclose the amount frozen.

Oct. 29 at 11:35 pm UTC

Binance says $2.54 billion frozen after hack

Binance said the verified total of assets frozen in connection with the hack had reached $2.54 billion, clarifying differing figures circulating publicly, including references to $1.8 billion.

The exchange said the total could increase as its teams work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets. Binance said it would publish further figures once verified.

Oct. 29 at 10:36 pm UTC

World Liberty Financial freezes $27 million in USD1 

World Liberty Financial has frozen $27 million in US-dollar-pegged stablecoin USD1 and $2 million worth of WLFI, according to Binance co-founder Yi He. 

“USD1 has taken proactive steps to freeze the $27 million in USD1 associated with the Binance hack,” said World Liberty Financial co-founder and CEO Zach Witkoff. 

World Liberty Financial said it worked with BitGo to freeze the stolen WLFI and USD1 funds. 

“We will cooperate fully with the ongoing investigation and support efforts to hold those responsible accountable. Protecting our users remains a top priority,” said World Liberty in a post on X. 

Oct. 29 at 10:33 pm UTC

Binance says withdrawals will resume once issues resolved

Binance says its team is conducting security checks and will resume withdrawals as soon as the “security issue” is resolved.

Oct. 29 at 10:32 pm UTC

Aave freezes markets after Binance exploiter borrows $44.6 million

Decentralized lending protocol Aave froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments as a precaution following the Binance hack.

In a governance forum update posted after the freeze, risk service provider LlamaRisk said the Binance exploiter deposited 60 million USDT and borrowed 19,762 Wrapped Ether (WETH), worth about $44.6 million at the time.

The borrowing occurred between 8:58 pm and 9:01 pm UTC on Oct. 29, about 40 minutes before the first freeze. It was the exploiter’s only Aave position across all networks and versions, with no further interactions detected after 9:01 pm UTC.

The position remained backed by $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt at the update’s snapshot. LlamaRisk said it remained subject to normal liquidation and did not put Aave suppliers at risk.

The freezes covered 175 reserves on V3 across 16 networks and 117 reserves on V4 across four networks.

Users can still withdraw funds and repay loans, and liquidations continue. However, the freeze prevents new deposits and borrowing, including additional collateral deposits, leaving repayment as the only way to improve an existing position’s health factor.

LlamaRisk said markets would remain frozen until the exploiter’s funds stopped moving and Binance provided greater clarity on containment, followed by a staged reopening. It warned that a prolonged freeze could push borrowing rates higher as withdrawals reduce available liquidity.

Oct. 29 at 9:19 pm UTC

Binance investigates multibillion-dollar security breach

Binance is investigating a potential multibillion-dollar security breach involving one of its Ethereum wallets, after suspicious transfers prompted stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle to reportedly freeze billions in assets.

A Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph on Thursday that the exchange was investigating reports of a potential security issue but had not confirmed any impact on user funds. The spokesperson said its security teams were reviewing the activity and would provide updates once more information was verified.

Concerns were first raised by blockchain researcher Spreek, who posted on X that assets from a Binance-linked Ethereum wallet had been transferred to a newly created address through a contract call allegedly funded by Tornado Cash. Spreek later reported that wallets connected to the transfers had begun selling Tether USDt (USDT) through decentralized exchanges.

Blockchain analytics platform Arkham Intelligence later identified a collection of wallets labeled “binance-hacker-1029” holding approximately $5.84 billion in digital assets. The figure represents the wallets’ reported holdings rather than a confirmed estimate of stolen funds.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the activity appeared to be a hack, adding that Tether and Circle had frozen approximately $971 million and $823 million, respectively. Zhao said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.

Source: Arkham Intelligence

Tether, Circle freeze over $2.36 billion

Blockchain security firm Blockaid said its team had identified roughly $3.3 billion in suspicious transfers involving Binance-linked wallets across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche.

Shortly after news of the hack emerged, Tether and Circle, the two largest stablecoin issuers by market capitalization, said they had frozen a combined $2.36 billion in tokens linked to the suspected incident.

Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement and would continue supporting the investigation.

A few minutes later, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT linked to the potential exploit.

“Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority,” Ardoino wrote.

The Binance hack came hours after Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a compromise at a third-party provider. The prediction market platform said it had fixed the issue and pledged to reimburse affected users, with all systems reported operational by 7:05 p.m. UTC Thursday.

title: FalconX Backs $250M Credit Facility for Ibis as Crypto Lending Infrastructure Evolves
summary: Onchain credit company Ibis emerged from stealth on October 28, announcing a $250 million credit facility with FalconX and a pre-seed funding round. For a.
content:
TL;DR: Onchain credit company Ibis emerged from stealth on October 28, announcing a $250 million credit facility with FalconX and a pre-seed funding round. For a crypto market accustomed to cycles of unsecured or poorly understood lending, the phrase institutional credit needs to be earned.

Onchain credit company Ibis emerged from stealth on October 28, announcing a $250 million credit facility with FalconX and a pre-seed funding round. The company says its initial borrowers will include eligible firms active in crypto trading and capital markets. Anchorage Digital Bank is named as a custody, banking and design partner, with other investors and advisers supporting the business. A committed credit facility defines potential lending capacity; it should not be reported as $250 million of loans already originated or as the company’s cash revenue.

The event and the market response

Ibis plans to originate, structure, tokenize, service and manage risk for institutional credit agreements. Its pitch is that digital-asset trading businesses can have sophisticated revenue and collateral profiles while conventional lenders lack frameworks to evaluate them. Combining underwriting with tokenized records may make credit positions easier to track or distribute to capital providers, but the economic risk does not disappear when documents become digital. The borrower’s ability to repay, enforceable collateral arrangements and a lender’s rights in default remain the basis of the product.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

For a crypto market accustomed to cycles of unsecured or poorly understood lending, the phrase institutional credit needs to be earned. A $250 million headline may suggest confidence, but lending discipline depends on covenants, concentration limits and transparent collateral controls when markets fall. Ibis’s structure could support a more professional market if those protections work in practice. The key distinction is between credit availability as an announcement and durable repayment performance through a stressful trading environment.

Tokenized finance is often described as a single market, but it covers quite different instruments: cash-like balances, securities, private credit and other claims. Each has different settlement and counterparty risks. Institutional adoption becomes meaningful when service providers can explain who owes what, how a holder exits a position and what happens during a dispute. The detail matters as much as speed. A sound launch can be the beginning of a larger change, although the step from successful integration to widespread, economically useful activity is rarely automatic.

The distinction between a blockchain record and the economic rights behind it is crucial for anyone evaluating this news. Digital tokens may move quickly, but title, custody, investor eligibility and redemption remain governed by legal agreements and regulated entities. A new integration should therefore be judged by the processes it can complete end to end, not simply by the number of assets it can represent. Traders also need to resist treating institutional enthusiasm as an automatic bullish signal for a native cryptocurrency: commercial adoption and token pricing can diverge for long periods.

What the headline does not establish

The press release says the platform may expand beyond crypto markets into other capital-hungry technology segments, including computing infrastructure and robotics. Those ambitions are not the same as live lending programs in each field. The confirmed starting point is the FalconX facility, the backing of named partners and Ibis’s proposed credit platform. Important details not fully specified in the announcement include loan pricing, advance rates, eligibility tests, actual utilization and how a tokenized claim would behave under insolvency. Institutions will demand clarity on those issues.

What to watch next

Track how much of the facility is drawn, the types of collateral accepted and evidence of repayments or portfolio performance. Those details will establish whether the structure becomes a repeatable market rather than an attractive launch headline.

title: Polymarket Links Trading Suspension to Third-Party Security Incident
summary:
Polymarket temporarily
halted trading on its international platform after a third-party provider was
compromised. The company said it had identified and fixed the issue, referred
the incident to law enforcement and would compensate affected users. Trading
was expected to resume around 3 p.m. ET on T...
content:
2026-10-29T22:07:12.450+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 20:07 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Blockchain activity linked a suspected attacker’s wallet to more than $2.5 million across 900 transactions.
  • Polymarket switched to cancel-only mode while investigating reports of drained user accounts.

Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform after a third-party provider was compromised. The company said it had identified and fixed the issue, referred the incident to law enforcement and would compensate affected users. Trading was expected to resume around 3 p.m. ET on Thursday, according to the company's announcement.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The suspension followed reports from users that funds had been drained from their accounts. The incident was linked to DebugBear, a performance-monitoring provider whose code was used on Polymarket's website, according to The Wall Street Journal. DebugBear said it was responding to a security incident and advised customers to remove its embedded code.

title: Bitwise Sees Bitcoin at $1.6 Million by 2036, but the Forecast Has Big Assumptions
summary: Bitwise Asset Management has raised its long-range Bitcoin price projection to $1.6 million by 2036 in its 2027 capital-market assumptions. The headline.
content:
TL;DR: Bitwise Asset Management has raised its long-range Bitcoin price projection to $1.6 million by 2036 in its 2027 capital-market assumptions. The headline will attract attention because it implies a dramatic rise from current levels, but the market should distinguish an investment thesis from a catalyst.

Bitwise Asset Management has raised its long-range Bitcoin price projection to $1.6 million by 2036 in its 2027 capital-market assumptions. The firm models annualized growth of 34.3% over the coming decade, based on institutional allocations, demand for scarce assets and constrained new issuance. It says this is an increase from a previous $1.3 million target. A forecast is not a traded price, and those numbers reflect the manager’s own scenario rather than an independently established future outcome. Investors should read the projection alongside the assumptions that could make it wrong.

The event and the market response

Among the inputs Bitwise highlights is the scale of institutional portfolios, which the firm places around $147 trillion. It argues that a potential allocation of 1% to 5% could imply between $1.5 trillion and $7 trillion of additional demand over time. Those figures are hypothetical allocations, not capital already committed to Bitcoin. The supply argument is more mechanical, reflecting the issuance schedule of the network, but price still depends on buyers and sellers at each moment. Supply scarcity alone cannot determine a future dollar valuation.

Why the development matters to the crypto market

The headline will attract attention because it implies a dramatic rise from current levels, but the market should distinguish an investment thesis from a catalyst. Bitwise has an interest in institutional Bitcoin adoption and its report is intended for long-horizon capital planning. Near-term traders still face macroeconomic news, ETF flows and leverage-driven price moves that may bear little resemblance to a ten-year projection. The proper use of a model this ambitious is to test sensitivities, not to treat the endpoint as a guaranteed destination.

The connection between digital assets and traditional finance is now too substantial for investors to ignore. Dollar financing rates, the appetite for technology shares, brokerage activity and institutional allocation decisions can all influence crypto demand. None of those relationships is fixed, however: correlation changes as investors rotate between risk and cash. Using a single session to support a dramatic long-term prediction is tempting but unreliable. Readers are better served by a sober distinction between published facts, market observations and forecasts that depend on uncertain assumptions.

What the headline does not establish

The manager also argues that Bitcoin’s characteristic four-year swings may moderate as ownership becomes more institutional. It points to a drawdown in 2026 that it portrays as shallower than previous historical cycles. That observation is compatible with maturation, but it does not establish that leverage, liquidity shocks or regulation can no longer produce violent corrections. Bitwise itself expects volatility to continue. An investor considering the model should ask what happens if adoption grows more slowly, institutions reduce positions, or other stores of value remain more attractive.

What to watch next

Readers can evaluate the forecast as new institutional ownership data, ETF flows and corporate treasury disclosures emerge. A useful check is whether the evidence matches the modeled adoption path rather than whether Bitcoin briefly moves closer to the final price target.

Primary source: Official statement / source documentation.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, prediction market platform Kalshi raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation, cryptocurrency exchange HTX agreed to halt unlawful promotions in the UK following legal action by the Financial Conduct Authority and CFTC Chair Michael Selig outlined a future where AI-powered refrigerators could stake Ether and launch memecoins.

Kalshi hits $40 billion valuation after $1 billion funding round

Prediction market platform Kalshi has raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation, nearly doubling since May as it expands beyond sports contracts.

Wellington Management and Sequoia Capital co-led the Series G round, Reuters reported Thursday. Kalshi also disclosed that its non-sports markets have surpassed $1 billion in annualized revenue, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The latest financing follows a $1 billion raise in May that valued Kalshi at $22 billion. The platform has since recorded approximately $15.8 billion in trading volume over the past 30 days, according to DefiLlama.

Kalshi is also expanding its commercial partnerships. Earlier this week, the NBA named Kalshi and rival Polymarket as preferred prediction market exchanges, while S&P Dow Jones Indices partnered with Kalshi to introduce financial benchmarks to event contracts.

The expansion comes amid mounting legal scrutiny of Kalshi’s sports contracts. Utah filed criminal charges against the company and its co-founders Wednesday over alleged illegal gambling activities, escalating a dispute over whether prediction markets fall under federal derivatives oversight or state gambling laws. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has separately moved to block Utah’s enforcement efforts.

HTX agrees to halt unlawful UK crypto promotions after FCA case

Cryptocurrency exchange HTX has agreed to stop unlawfully promoting its services to consumers in the United Kingdom under a settlement announced Thursday by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).

Huobi Global S.A., the Panamanian company behind HTX, agreed that it would not knowingly run illegal promotions, including through the exchange’s website, apps or social media. The court undertakings run until Oct. 21, 2031.

The settlement terms are confidential, and the agreement does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing.

“Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law,” said Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA. “The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.”

In an Oct. 16 notice outlining its UK exit arrangements, the exchange formerly known as Huobi said existing UK accounts could no longer deposit or trade. Eligible users can request a one-time 48-hour window to withdraw remaining assets, subject to approval and compliance checks. Accounts will close after all assets have been withdrawn.

The FCA brought the case in October 2025 and announced it in February, which it said was the agency’s first enforcement action against a crypto firm over illegal marketing.

Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins: CFTC chair

Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig says it is “no longer science fiction” to imagine one’s refrigerator autonomously purchasing groceries with money earned from staking Ether — or even launching its own memecoin, raising questions about how regulators should oversee autonomous AI agents.

The colorful comment came during Selig’s remarks at the CFTC’s inaugural Frontier Forum in Washington, DC, on Wednesday, where he argued that regulators must adapt to a financial system where AI agents can hold assets and execute trades autonomously.

“We’re gathered here today to discuss a technology that’s rapidly transforming the financial markets. President Trump calls it ‘super intelligence,’ or SI, because ‘it’s not artificial.’ It’s as real as the printing press, the steam engine, and the internet,” he said.

The regulatory questions come as younger investors embrace AI tools for managing money. An eToro survey published in September found that 79% of US millennial investors and 77% of Gen Z investors already used or were open to using AI to select or adjust their investments, highlighting the potential reach of rules governing automated finance.

title: Public companies double share of blockchain revenue since 2022: Report
summary: A new 1kx report finds that public companies are capturing a larger share of blockchain revenue, driven by institutional adoption and real-world applications.
content:
Publicly traded companies accounted for 16% of blockchain industry revenue in 2026, more than double their 7% share in 2022, according to a new report from crypto investment firm 1kx.

The increase comes as overall blockchain revenue is projected to decline 28% year over year to roughly $100 billion in 2026. The report analyzed data from more than 2,600 protocols and earnings reports from 104 publicly traded companies through the third quarter.

The researchers attributed the growing share of public companies partly to new stock market listings, including stablecoin issuer Circle, which went public in 2025, and revenue growth among existing companies. The 10 largest publicly traded companies in the study doubled their blockchain-related revenue over the past three years.

Coinbase and Circle generated approximately $3.3 billion in combined blockchain-related revenue in the first half of 2026, according to 1kx, while publicly traded Bitcoin miners earned roughly $2 billion. Traditional financial firms, including JPMorgan, BlackRock, CME Group, Visa and Robinhood, accounted for another $1.1 billion collectively.

Revenue remains concentrated among a relatively small number of businesses. The six largest publicly traded companies accounted for roughly 50% to 60% of the group’s revenue, according to the report.

Related: BlackRock files for third Bitcoin ETF, still no Solana or XRP

Institutional and real-world activity gains share of blockchain revenue

The report also found that revenue from broader economic activity surpassed blockchain infrastructure revenue for the first time in the third quarter, reaching approximately $5.3 billion compared with $5.1 billion, according to 1kx.

The category, which includes tokenized assets, payments and prediction markets, grew 58% year over year in the first half of 2026. Together with institutional adoption, it accounted for 33% of total blockchain revenue in the third quarter, with the report projecting a 30% share for the full year.

Institutional and broader economic activity to reach 30% of blockchain revenue in 2026. Source: 1kx report

RWA.xyz data shows the value of distributed tokenized real-world assets rose roughly 51% over the past year, from $26.16 billion in October 2025 to $39.54 billion as of Thursday. Tokenized equities grew even faster, surging 471% over the same period to $3.77 billion.

title: Polymarket suspended trading amid reports of user funds being drained
summary: The prediction markets platform halted trading on Thursday after it reported one of its third party providers had been compromised.
content:
The prediction markets platform halted trading on Thursday after it reported one of its third party providers had been compromised.

Prediction markets company Polymarket reported its Predictions Trading API had experienced a “major outage,” resulting in the platform temporarily halting trading.

In a Thursday update to its status page, Polymarket said that the platform was in “cancel-only” mode after it had identified and fixed an issue impacting its operations. As of 7:05 pm UTC, the platform reported all its systems were operational.

“One of our third party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement,” said Polymarket. “Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole.”

The suspension of trading came as several users claimed online that their Polymarket accounts had been drained of thousands of dollars after their positions were sold without their consent. In June, Polymarket reported that hackers were able to drain more than $2.9 million in user funds by compromising a third-party vendor.

summary:

Claude and ChatGPT, to their accounts for analysis and, with the required
permissions, trade execution.
London's trading indu...
content:
2026-10-29T20:06:04.337+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 18:06 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • External AI agents with full access can execute permitted trades without individual order confirmations.
  • The update follows similar MCP integrations by Leverate, Freedom24, ThinkMarkets and cTrader.

B2BROKER Group has added Model Context Protocol support and an in-terminal AI chat to its B2TRADER platform. The update allows traders to connect external AI tools, including Claude and ChatGPT, to their accounts for analysis and, with the required permissions, trade execution.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Other trading platforms have introduced similar integrations. In September, Leverate introduced an MCP connection that allows traders to use ChatGPT or Claude to analyse accounts and prepare orders, subject to trader confirmation. CMC Markets also connected UK CFD accounts to ChatGPT, but restricted the integration to read-only access.

In August, Finance Magnates reported that Freedom24 had added AI access to its Tradernet platform, while ThinkMarkets and cTrader also adopted MCP-based integrations.

B2BROKER Expands AI From Analysis to Execution

B2BROKER introduced an embedded AI Assistant for B2TRADER earlier this year, offering market forecasts, sentiment indicators, recommendation scores and trading signals. A subsequent update added external market statistics and third-party asset news.

The latest release extends these features to account-specific analysis and trade execution . Connected AI agents can retrieve market data, review portfolios and account history, and follow instructions such as closing profitable positions or setting stop-loss orders.

Brokers determine the level of access available to connected agents. Read-only access allows analysis and monitoring but excludes trading functions. Full access permits agents to place, modify and close trades. Brokers can also disable MCP, and each agent is restricted to accounts belonging to the trader who authorised it.

B2BROKER Expects AI Chat to Cut Support Enquiries

The in-terminal AI Chat uses the same MCP layer, allowing traders to ask about markets, positions and platform features. Trading actions proposed through the chat require explicit confirmation. External agents with full access, however, can execute permitted trades without individual order confirmations.

“For brokers, adding AI to a terminal raises an immediate question: who decides what an assistant can actually do?” said Arthur Azizov, Founder and CEO of B2BROKER Group.

B2BROKER expects the in-terminal chat to reduce routine first-line support enquiries. The company also said external AI connectivity could help brokers differentiate their platforms when attracting clients.

Broker AI Integrations Range From Monitoring to Execution

A June report by Finance Magnates Intelligence examined AI integrations across brokers and trading platforms. It found that Claude was supported by nine of the ten integrations studied and compared access models ranging from account monitoring to human-approved orders and AI-driven trade execution.

title: FutureBit Apollo Solo Miner Finds Bitcoin Block 973262, Earning 3.154 BTC
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

FutureBit Apollo Solo Miner Finds Bitcoin Block 973262, Earning 3.154 BTC
A miner running FutureBit’s Apollo Solo setup found Bitcoin block 973,262 on Oct. 26, collecting the full 3.154 BTC subsidy-plus-fees reward from 2,477 transactions.
This post FutureBit Apollo Solo Miner Find...
content:
A miner operating through FutureBit’s Apollo Solo setup found Bitcoin block 973,262 earlier this week, collecting the full reward of 3.154 BTC plus fees from 2,477 transactions. Multiple explorers, including mempool.space, list the finder as “FutureBit Apollo Solo,” and the coinbase transaction includes text referencing FutureBit and Apollo.

FutureBit posted about the find on X: “Gradually, then suddenly. We (the people) hit a Bitcoin block today. Bitcoin belongs in the hands of sovereign individuals. And we’re building to keep it there.” The company stated that an Apollo device or Solo Node running its built-in solo pool assembled the block template, served the work, and submitted the completed block to the network. The public record does not identify the exact hardware or hashrate that produced the winning hash. It could have been an Apollo BTC, Apollo II, Apollo III, or other compatible machines pointed at a Solo Node, according to FutureBit’s account of the block. 

This marks at least the fourth block attributed to FutureBit Apollo Solo. Earlier ones include blocks 867,760, 881,423, and 888,737. FutureBit designs its Apollo hardware for operators who want to run a full Bitcoin node and mine independently at home rather than through large commercial pools. The most recent model, the Apollo III, is rated for up to 18 TH/s in turbo mode with an integrated full node. Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III launch in February 2026 and previously examined FutureBit’s approach to home mining in a July 2025 piece.

Solo mining, is often called lottery mining because of the low odds relative to the size of the reward, remains uncommon against a network hashrate that has recently sat near 1,070–1,087 EH/s. A home-scale setup in the 10–18 TH/s range still faces expected times to a block measured in centuries under current difficulty, yet verified solo finds continue to appear on-chain. Bitcoin Magazine examined the mathematics of these odds in an article titled Why Bitcoin Lottery Mining Has Better Odds Than The Powerball. It compared continuous Bitcoin block attempts with the much lower frequency of major lottery draws.

Another solo block was found the following day via CKPool Solo,  illustrating that individual operators can still capture full rewards even as industrial pools produce the large majority of blocks. For users running FutureBit hardware, the company notes that the individual users control both the node and the solo pool, retaining the full reward when a block is found. Solo mining also has significant privacy benefits, and hardware and energy costs can be written off against taxes in some jurisdictions.

The October 26 block is one more validation that solo mining can be viable. Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design intended the full Bitcoin node to be able to mine blocks, not just validate and audit the blockchain. Improvements in hardware and mining optimizations later on led to the creation of mining pools, which created a very competitive and industrial mining sector. The secondary effects of industrial Bitcoin mining, such as reliable energy demand that can stabilize the grid, have been a boon for states like Texas. 

However, the dream of bringing mining back to homes and end users remains alive through companies like FutureBit, Bitaxe, and HeatBit, among others, that are converting heating appliances into Bitcoin miners or designing hardware of the sort for the home.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4 AI Models With Native Audio and Photorealistic Simulations
summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4, expanding its artificial intelligence portfolio with advances in cybersecurity, software development, and interactive world simulation.
content:
Skip to content

Google has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4, expanding its artificial intelligence portfolio with advances in cybersecurity, software development, and interactive world simulation.

Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon focuses on complex reasoning, secure code generation, and long-running agentic tasks, while Genie 4 creates interactive environments with photorealistic visuals and native audio.

The announcements highlight two distinct areas of AI development. Carbon targets demanding technical and security workloads, while Genie 4 aims to generate dynamic digital worlds that respond to user instructions in real time. Both models are being introduced through limited-access programs before broader availability.

Gemini 4 Carbon Tops Intelligence and Cybersecurity Benchmarks

Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced Gemini 4 Carbon as the newest frontier model in the Gemini 4 family. Its release follows Gemini 4 Argon, which arrived approximately two weeks earlier, underscoring the pace of development within Google’s AI lineup.

Gemini 4 Carbon delivers improved performance over its predecessor Argon, with advanced cybersecurity capabilities and enhanced support for long-running agentic tasks. Source: Google via X

According to the supplied benchmark results, Carbon ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, scoring 59 points. The model also records strong results across several cybersecurity evaluations, including 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability detection, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71.0% on CWE-bench for software patching.

These benchmarks assess different capabilities, from identifying security weaknesses to evaluating how effectively a model can address vulnerabilities. Their results offer measurable indicators of performance, although scores across separate evaluations do not necessarily translate directly into better outcomes in every real-world environment.

Google also reports substantial improvements over Gemini 4 Argon in long-horizon tasks, agentic coding, and multimodal understanding. Secure code generation reportedly delivers a twofold improvement, while the model’s safeguards are designed to reduce susceptibility to indirect prompt injection attacks.

The supplied announcement describes Carbon as achieving perfect resistance to indirect prompt injection in the reported evaluation. This result should be understood within the scope of that test rather than as proof of immunity to every prompt injection technique or cybersecurity threat.

Gemini 4 Carbon Demonstrates Advanced 3D Modeling Capabilities

Gemini 4 Carbon has also attracted attention for its performance in computer-aided design (CAD) and complex 3D modeling. A side-by-side video shared by AI tracker @Mr_Salio compares the model with Opus 5.5 on a detailed airplane-design task.

The post compares Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon with Opus 5.5 in a side-by-side video demonstration of complex 3D airplane modeling. Source: @Mr_Salio via X

The demonstration focuses on technically demanding features, including X-ray views, exploded assemblies, and intricate internal components. The aircraft models reportedly contain between 1,400 and more than 2,600 parts, requiring the system to maintain structural consistency across numerous connected elements.

In the comparison, Carbon appears to handle internal assemblies and complex views with greater coherence and detail. Such capabilities could be useful for engineering visualization, product design, and other workflows in which models must preserve relationships between components.

However, a demonstration video alone does not establish how consistently a model performs across professional CAD workloads. Independent testing would be needed to assess dimensional accuracy, editability, engineering constraints, and reliability in production environments.

Google Begins Gemini 4 Carbon Rollout Through Fairwind

Google is initially making Gemini 4 Carbon available to selected cybersecurity professionals through its Fairwind Program. The staged rollout is intended to gather feedback on the model’s capabilities, safety measures, and suitability for security-related tasks before wider access.

Google is gradually releasing Gemini 4 Carbon to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program, with enhanced safeguards against prompt injection and model misalignment ahead of wider access. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

The approach reflects the challenges of releasing powerful AI systems that can assist with vulnerability discovery and software security. These capabilities may help defenders identify weaknesses and develop fixes, but they also require safeguards against misuse.

Google plans to expand access to developers and other users in the near future. The supplied announcement lists introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. These figures represent the stated initial rates, which may be subject to the terms of the eventual public release.

The company also highlights improvements in resistance to prompt injection and reductions in misalignment rates. The effectiveness of these protections will depend on how the model behaves across different applications, attack methods, and deployment conditions.

Genie 4 Generates Photorealistic Worlds With Native Audio

Alongside Carbon, Google DeepMind has introduced Genie 4, an interactive world model designed to generate dynamic environments with realistic visuals, physical movement, and synchronized audio.

Google DeepMind unveiled Genie 4, an interactive world model that generates photorealistic simulations with native audio and maintains consistency through Gemini integration. Source: Google via X

Unlike a conventional video generator that produces a fixed sequence of frames, an interactive world model allows users to influence what happens inside a generated environment. Genie 4 supports real-time text instructions that can change scenes, camera angles, and actions as a simulation unfolds.

Native audio is another central feature. Generated environments can include ambient sounds, music, engine noise, and character dialogue, adding an audio layer that responds to events within the simulated world.

Google’s demonstrations illustrate how these capabilities work together. In one 50-second example, a first-person motorcycle journey begins at a red traffic light on a sunlit coastal highway. A text instruction changes the light to green, after which the motorcycle accelerates along the road. Engine revs, ocean waves, and passing traffic accompany the movement.

Other demonstrations reportedly include dragon flights, crowded train stations, and robotic systems handling liquids. These examples showcase the model’s ability to combine visual detail, physical interactions, and changing scene conditions.

Gemini integration also helps Genie 4 track the state of its simulated environment and coordinate multi-step events. This is important for maintaining continuity as objects move, actions unfold, and users modify the scene.

Genie 4 Access Expands Through Project Genie and Gemini API

Genie 4 is currently available as a research preview for trusted testers. Google plans to extend access to Google AI Ultra subscribers through Project Genie, while selected partners are expected to receive early access through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

Sundar Pichai unveiled Genie 4, Google’s advanced world model featuring real-time environment control, dynamic actions, and native audio with realistic dialogue. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

The limited rollout gives Google an opportunity to evaluate the system before making it more widely available. As with other generative AI tools, practical performance will depend on the complexity of the requested environment, the consistency of interactions, and the model’s ability to preserve realistic behavior over time.

Interactive world models could support several applications beyond entertainment. In robotics, generated environments may help researchers test control systems and explore scenarios that would be expensive, difficult, or unsafe to reproduce physically. Developers could also use the technology for simulation, virtual prototyping, and interactive experiences.

Nevertheless, simulated environments do not automatically reproduce every constraint of the physical world. Robotics and engineering applications will require careful validation to determine whether generated scenarios provide sufficiently accurate conditions for training and testing.

Google Advances AI Across Coding and Interactive Simulation

Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4 address different but complementary areas of AI development. Carbon emphasizes reasoning, cybersecurity, and complex technical workflows, while Genie 4 focuses on generating interactive worlds with realistic visuals, physics, and sound.

Their initial releases remain limited, and broader availability will provide more opportunities to evaluate performance outside curated demonstrations and benchmark environments. For Carbon, key questions include how reliably it detects vulnerabilities and produces secure code. For Genie 4, the focus will be on consistency, real-time responsiveness, and the accuracy of simulated interactions.

Google’s announcements illustrate a wider effort to develop AI systems that can do more than generate text or images. By combining advanced reasoning with specialized capabilities, the company is targeting applications ranging from software security and engineering to simulation and robotics. The models’ practical value will ultimately depend on their reliability, safety, and performance in real-world use.

title: HYPE teases all-time high as NYSE owner ICE eyes US Hyperliquid perps
summary: Hyperliquid’s token pumped following news of ICE and Trade[XYZ] unveiling plans for US perpetual futures.
content:
Hyperliquid’s native token HYPE surged about 20% Thursday after New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) announced plans for US perpetual futures with Trade[XYZ], whose investors include billionaire Wall Street investor Stanley Druckenmiller.

HYPE traded above $96 at the time of writing, up by around 20% in the past 24 hours, according to CoinGecko, flirting with September’s all-time record of $97.96.

Perpetual futures allow traders to take positions on asset prices without an expiration date. Hyperliquid is the largest decentralized exchange in the world to trade such instruments, DefiLlama data shows.

The companies said Thursday they would seek regulatory approval for markets covering cryptocurrencies, stocks, indexes, commodities and currencies. The proposed market would target retail traders. ICE said it would operate separately from its institutional futures business, with a dedicated clearing structure.

More than 99% of participation in its markets is institutional, ICE said, with the separate clearing structure intended to shield existing customers from retail counterparty risks.

The proposal would give US retail traders a regulated route to Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures, and ICE a new route into retail trading. President Donald Trump said on Aug. 19 that Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the country in a “fully compliant and legal fashion.” 

Related: Wall Street wealth creation model is unsustainable for most participants: Hyperliquid CEO

Druckenmiller investment draws Musk reaction

“I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz),” Druckenmiller wrote on X, adding that he looked forward to using its products.

Elon Musk also drew attention to the agreement, sharing Druckenmiller’s post with the one-word comment “Interesting.”

ICE is taking a minority stake in Trade[XYZ], but disclosed neither the investment amount nor a launch date. Cointelegraph reached out to ICE and Trade[XYZ] for comment but had not received a response by publication.

Customers would undergo identity and Anti-Money-Laundering checks and trade through participating futures brokers.

Distribution is expected through ICE’s joint venture with OKX, pending separate approvals. ICE invested in OKX at a $25 billion valuation in March. 

Related: ICE, CME press US regulators to ‘rein in’ Hyperliquid energy trading: Report

OKX venture faces issuer objections

Meanwhile, ICE’s separate tokenized stock venture with OKX has disclosed objections from 38 companies, up from 26 reported by Cointelegraph on Oct. 27. 

Its Oct. 28 notice adds Walmart, Eli Lilly, Carnival, Arcos Dorados and Cigna. However, those objections concern tokenized shares, while the Trade[XYZ] proposal involves perpetual futures and remains subject to separate regulatory approvals.

The regulatory opening remains conditional. The CFTC approved Kalshi’s Bitcoin perpetual contract in May, but said perpetuals referencing other asset classes should receive case-by-case review.

title: ICE Partners With Trade[XYZ] to Bring $650B Hyperliquid Futures Market to the U.S.
summary:
Key Takeaways: ICE and Trade[XYZ] prepare to launch a U.S. perpetual futures market, pending approval from the CFTC. Hyperliquid’s trading volume in Trade[XYZ] is more than $650 billion through, in
The post ICE Partners With Trade[XYZ] to Bring $650B Hyperliquid Futures Market to the U.S. appeared f...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • ICE and Trade[XYZ] prepare to launch a U.S. perpetual futures market, pending approval from the CFTC.
  • Hyperliquid’s trading volume in Trade[XYZ] is more than $650 billion through, in the span of little over a year.
  • Planned contracts are available for cryptocurrencies, stocks, indices, commodity and foreign exchange.

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, is partnering with Trade[XYZ] to bring round-the-clock perpetual futures trading to the U.S. The proposed platform will leverage Hyperliquid’s market technology infrastructure, while harnessing ICE’s experience in regulated exchanges and clearing.

trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid.

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

— trade.xyz (@tradexyz) October 29, 2026

  • ICE Targets U.S. Access to 24/7 Crypto Futures
  • Trade[XYZ] Reports $650B in Hyperliquid Volume
    • ICE Makes Strategic Investment in Trade[XYZ]
    • Hyperliquid Gains a Potential U.S. Market Gateway

ICE Targets U.S. Access to 24/7 Crypto Futures

The companies plan to create a separate market for perpetual futures on the U.S. exchange, subject to approval from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The planned place would provide contracts based on cryptocurrencies and traditional assets such as stocks, stock indexes, commodities, foreign exchange, etc.

Permanent contracts are not terminated and expire unlike normal futures. They enable traders to hold positions over margin limits and usually the trader pays money to keep contract prices in line with the underlying market price.

The platform being proposed will help make this model of trading more regulated in the U.S. Access will be available via participating brokers and platforms, and the companies haven’t yet released a launch date or finalized details on products and customer eligibility.

ICE will offer the functions of exchange operations, clearing and risk management expertise. Trade[XYZ] will offer its product design and technology in markets, developed on Hyperliquid.

Read More: 22 Companies Block OKXICE Tokenized Stocks, Putting 63-Share Crypto Plan Under Pressure

Trade[XYZ] Reports $650B in Hyperliquid Volume

In less than a year, Trade[XYZ] has seen over $650 billion worth of trading volume go through their markets. Users can trade perpetual contracts on assets like stocks, indexes and commodities, outside of traditional market hours, with its existing products.

The firm intends to keep expanding on these established markets in addition to the proposed venue in the U.S. With that would come continued expansion of its existing Hyperliquid business, while partners go through a different regulatory process with American customers.

ICE Makes Strategic Investment in Trade[XYZ]

ICE is also making a strategic investment in the private firm with both sides declining to say how much. Along with a handful of market movers, including investor Stan Druckenmiller, is the world’s largest group of them.

The partnership brings together ICE’s market infrastructures and Trade[XYZ]’s experience in creating markets on an 24×7 decentralized trading network. However, the plans for the product line for the eventual U.S. offering remain subject to regulatory approvals, and may depend on the approvals received.

Hyperliquid Gains a Potential U.S. Market Gateway

The agreement may provide Hyperliquid-perpetuals with structured access to U.S. clientele. It also highlights the increased activity among traditional finance institutions in crypto derivatives and trading platforms.

The integration of around-the-clock trading and U.S. exchange and clearing platforms is the major one for the crypto industry. The companies have not specified the timing for trading and the total amount of investment ICE will make into the market are not disclosed.
