title: Franklin Templeton Officially Launches 2 Bitcoin DRIP ETFs That Turn Dividends Into Bitcoin
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Franklin Templeton Officially Launches 2 Bitcoin DRIP ETFs That Turn Dividends Into Bitcoin
Franklin Templeton’s two Bitcoin DRIP ETFs, FBEQ and FIBT, started trading today on the Nasdaq.
This post Franklin Templeton Officially Launches 2 Bitcoin DRIP ETFs That Turn Dividends Into ...
content:
Two Nasdaq-listed funds route dividends from large U.S. companies into a bitcoin sleeve that grows with every payment.

Franklin Templeton has officially launched two exchange-traded funds that convert stock dividends into bitcoin. The Franklin U.S. Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FBEQ) and the Franklin U.S. Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF (FIBT) will trade on Nasdaq. 

The launch completes the last regulatory step after Franklin filed registration papers with the Securities and Exchange Commission on October 22. The filings for both funds arrived in June without tickers or fees. Four months after that filing, the details are in. 

How the funds work

FBEQ tracks the VettaFi U.S. Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index. The index holds the 500 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, weighted by float-adjusted market cap. As of September 30, it held 499 stocks ranging from $10.2 billion to $5.5 trillion in size, with the heaviest concentration in information technology.

At inception, the index allocates 95% to those stocks and 5% to BTC. Each dividend the companies pay, whether regular or special, is reinvested into BTC at the market open on the day after the ex-date. The BTC share of the portfolio grows with each payment.

A traditional dividend reinvestment plan, or DRIP, uses cash dividends to buy more shares of the company that paid them. Franklin’s version routes that cash into BTC. For a holder, the dividend stream from the largest companies in America becomes a recurring BTC purchase, with no exchange account, no wallet and no custody decisions.

The bitcoin position has limits. At each quarterly rebalance, any allocation above 5% gets trimmed to 4.5%. If BTC exceeds 20% of the index between rebalances, the index cuts it to 4.5% within two business days, and the proceeds return to stocks. 

The result is a stock fund with a bitcoin sleeve, a different product from a BTC fund.

The fund holds no BTC on-chain. It gains exposure through BTC exchange-traded products, including Franklin’s own spot fund, through bitcoin futures and options, or through depositary receipts, in some cases via a Cayman Islands subsidiary.

FBEQ carries a 0.09% expense ratio and charges no 12b-1 fee. Franklin Advisory Services manages the fund, with Franklin Templeton Institutional as sub-advisor.

Bitcoin as a mature, investable asset

“Bitcoin has matured as an investable asset, supported by deeper market infrastructure, broader adoption and a growing understanding of the role it can play in portfolios,” said Dina Ting, SVP and Head of Index Investments at Franklin Templeton. “A systematic approach to building exposure is one way to address this next stage of adoption.”

Jeff Masom, Head of U.S. Distribution and Global Wealth Management Private Markets, framed the funds as a new way to combine U.S. equities and bitcoin through a differentiated index methodology.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: ECB President Christine Lagarde to Retire in July 2027
summary:
Key Takeaways: The ECB President, Christine Lagarde, will retire on February 7, 2027. The EU appointment process for her successor will start right away. The leadership transition has brought the
The post ECB President Christine Lagarde to Retire in July 2027 appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The ECB President, Christine Lagarde, will retire on February 7, 2027.
  • The EU appointment process for her successor will start right away.
  • The leadership transition has brought the ECB back into the limelight as crypto regulation and the use of stablecoins strengthen in Europe.

Christine Lagarde has confirmed she will leave the European Central Bank (ECB) before completing her full term, marking one of the biggest upcoming leadership changes in European finance. The announcement does not specify any new crypto policies, but the move coincides with a period where digital assets, stablecoins, and blockchain-based payments are growing in significance throughout the eurozone financial landscape.

I have just informed my colleagues that I will step down as @ECB President on 7 February 2027.

It has been a source of great pride to serve this institution.

I thank all of those who have supported me on this journey over the past seven years. https://t.co/eSLLTaDAej

— Christine Lagarde (@Lagarde) October 29, 2026

  • Lagarde Confirms Early Departure
  • Why Crypto Markets Will Watch the Next ECB Leader
    • Leadership Change Arrives During Europe’s Digital Finance Push
    • Succession Process Moves Into Focus

Lagarde Confirms Early Departure

On October 29, Lagarde announced she will resign on February 7, 2027, almost nine months before her tenure was set to expire in October 2027. The role of the ECB President was extremely rewarding and she thanked her colleagues who supported her in the last seven years, she said.

The ECB has already started preparations to make the transition. European Council President António Costa has announced that the process for selecting her successor will begin right away to ensure a seamless handover.

The statement was timed with the ECB’s own interest rate decision the same day to put extra pressure on Europe’s monetary main man.

Read More: Trump Crypto Empire Leaves Investors $4.7B Underwater, Public Citizen Report Claims

Why Crypto Markets Will Watch the Next ECB Leader

The ECB is still one of the most influential central banks in the world and its leadership also has a strong influence on European policy towards financial innovation and monetary policy.

Lagarde’s comments didn’t come with specific words for cryptocurrencies, but her successor will preside over the central bank just as the EU moves forward with digital-asset regulations, further developed oversight of stablecoins and continued progress on the digital euro.

The post-coming-in-in-logo ECB president will be a crucial figure to listen to in the talks on payment infrastructure, tokenized finance and financial stability for any crypto businesses that span across Europe.

Leadership Change Arrives During Europe’s Digital Finance Push

The change is also interesting as several other top roles at the ECB will be up for grabs within months of the others, giving one of the biggest reshuffles of leadership in years.

This shift syncs with rising institutional adoption of blockchain finance services, such as tokenized assets, and regulated stablecoins. Many firms including Ripple, Circle and top European banks have continued to ramp up their tokenisation efforts in payments and capital markets, increasing the importance of regulation.

Succession Process Moves Into Focus

The European Council will select the next ECB president in accordance with EU legislation that includes the backing of eurozone finance ministers, the European Parliament and the ECB’s Governing Council.  A number of candidates have featured in the wider media but no one has made official headlines.

This change does not just signal a policy change but a leadership shift which may impact Europe’s future digital finance outlook.

title: India Names Binance and Bybit Among Foreign Platforms in $585M Crypto Remittance Probe
summary:
India’s Enforcement
Directorate (ED) is investigating alleged cryptocurrency-linked cross-border
transactions worth around $585 million (₹5,000
crore). The case involves Mudrex, Saber.money and decentralised finance
protocol Instadapp.
On 27 October, the
agency searched four premises, including thre...
content:
2026-10-29T17:23:43.644+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 15:23 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The ED alleges that Mudrex and Saber.money’s operator used crypto for unauthorised transfers.
  • Instadapp’s DeFi protocol was allegedly managed from India despite being presented as a US-based business.

India’s Enforcement Directorate (ED) is investigating alleged cryptocurrency-linked cross-border transactions worth around $585 million (₹5,000 crore). The case involves Mudrex, Saber.money and decentralised finance protocol Instadapp.

On 27 October, the agency searched four premises, including three in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh, under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The operation follows an earlier ED investigation into CoinSwitch Kuber. In August 2022, the agency searched premises linked to the crypto exchange over suspected violations of India’s foreign exchange laws.

Binance, Bybit Named in $538M India Crypto Probe

The latest probe centres on RPFAS Technologies, which operates Mudrex and Saber.money. The ED alleges that the company facilitated overseas transfers without authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India.

Customers allegedly deposited fiat currency that was converted into stablecoins such as USDT and sold through crypto exchanges to transfer funds outside official banking channels.

The agency also identified overseas entities in the US, Canada and Lithuania, and named Binance and Bybit among the foreign exchanges involved in the transactions under investigation. It estimates the alleged FEMA violations linked to RPFAS Technologies at $538 million (₹4,600 crore).

BREAKING: 🇮🇳 ED searches 3 locations over alleged ₹5,000 crore crypto-linked illegal cross-border transactions involving Binance and Bybit. https://t.co/Jp2zo78Dkg

— Crypto India (@CryptooIndia) October 29, 2026

Instadapp Faces $40M India Foreign Exchange Probe

The investigation also covers Instadapp, which operates as Fluid. The ED alleges that founder Sowmay Jain managed the protocol from India, although the business was presented as a US-based operation.

According to the agency, stablecoin revenues passed through entities in the British Virgin Islands, Singapore and Dubai before being converted into fiat currency and transferred to India as payments for what it described as “bogus software development and consultancy fees”. The alleged FEMA violations involving Instadapp are estimated at $40 million (₹380 crore).

India’s Crypto Crackdown Includes Raids and Fines

India has also taken action against offshore crypto exchanges over anti-money laundering compliance. In December 2023, authorities moved to block access to nine platforms, including Binance. Binance and KuCoin registered with India’s Financial Intelligence Unit in 2024, with Binance subsequently fined ₹188.2 million for alleged anti-money laundering violations.

Separately, tax authorities raided six Indian crypto exchanges in January 2022, uncovering approximately $9.4 million in unpaid taxes, according to reports at the time.

The allegations in the current case have not been established as findings of guilt.

title: Russia Approves Securities Group to Oversee Crypto Exchanges
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Russia Approves Securities Group to Oversee Crypto Exchanges
The Bank of Russia approved NAUFOR as the country’s first self-regulatory organization for crypto exchanges and digital depositories.
This post Russia Approves Securities Group to Oversee Crypto Exchanges first appeared o...
content:
The National Association of Securities Market Participants, known as NAUFOR, has won self-regulatory organization status for digital depositories and crypto exchanges. The Central Bank of Russia made the decision on October 29, according to Interfax.

The move turns a law into a working system. Russia’s framework, “On Digital Currency and Digital Rights,” passed the State Duma in July. It requires exchange operators and depositories to sit in central bank registries, and it requires them to join an SRO. 

Interfax reports that the registry lists 23 crypto exchanges and eight digital depositories, including VTB, Sberbank, and units of T-Technologies, the holding company behind T-Bank. Firms on those registries have 90 days to join an SRO. In short, an SRO writes industry standards, monitors members, and represents the industry to regulators.

NAUFOR says it will help shape standards for digital asset markets and push the central bank on rule changes. Earlier in October, it received the same status for information system operators. The association has operated since 1996 and counts 725 members, including brokers, dealers, and fund managers from traditional markets.

Russia’s crypto legal gateway

Traditional finance built NAUFOR’s model for stocks and bonds. Placing the same body over bitcoin exchanges and custody gives the state a familiar hand on the wheel. 

Bitcoin Magazine reported in July that the law stops bitcoin from becoming money for everyday purchases. Domestic crypto payments stay banned. The law licenses exchanges and depositories, caps retail purchases, and opens a state-supervised channel for cross-border trade, a route that helps Russia move around Western sanctions.

The details matter for users. A depository would record holdings, and one reading of the framework lets it restrict transfers to personal wallets. Non-qualified retail buyers can purchase up to 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary, near $3,800. 

Qualified investors face higher ceilings. These choices shape who can use the platforms and how.

Earlier this fall, the Moscow Exchange reportedly began testing cryptocurrency trading with professional market participants and planned to launch trading this December. 

The exchange intended to use existing infrastructure and a partner digital depository following the introduction of Russia’s new cryptocurrency regulations in September. 

Sberbank also received approval to custody Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, while President Vladimir Putin had previously acknowledged Bitcoin’s resistance to being banned.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions Crypto Launderers Behind North Korea’s Fake Workers
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Sanctions Crypto Launderers Behind North Korea’s Fake Workers
The U.S. Treasury sanctioned ten people and one entity, including two Russian crypto middlemen, for laundering money from North Korean fake IT worker schemes that fund its weapons programs.
This post U.S. T...
content:
The U.S. Treasury Department on Tuesday sanctioned ten individuals and one company, accusing them of helping North Korea collect wages from foreign employers, many of them American, through fake identities and forged paperwork.

The workers are typically placed at legitimate firms under invented personas, sometimes with AI-generated resumes, doctored photos, or deepfake video during interviews. 

Most of their pay goes back to the regime, which Treasury says uses the money to fund its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs. Some of these workers have also gained access to corporate networks, where they have planted malware and taken proprietary data.

The money and crypto behind North Korean fraud

The sanctions focused less on the workers themselves than on the people who move the money. Two Russian nationals are at the center of the action. 

Vitold Obertas, described by Treasury as a go-between for North Korean financial transactions, allegedly handled nearly $2 million in crypto conversions and at least $1.25 million in other currency transfers for North Korean officials since January 2025. 

Ilya Boykov allegedly converted the equivalent of $3.5 million in crypto for Alis, a North Korean IT worker company that the U.S. sanctioned in 2024.

Two North Korean nationals, Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong, were also named for leading Russia-based worker delegations. Kim Ki Hyok has reportedly moved close to $500,000 in crypto for his team since 2024. 

Treasury also sanctioned the First Financial and Technical Development Center, a North Korean-controlled entity operating in Russia, along with six workers who have generated more than $750,000 for it since 2025.

Treasury published wallet addresses on Ethereum and Tron tied to the sanctioned individuals, a signal to exchanges and other financial firms to watch for those accounts. One Ethereum address is linked to both Obertas and Boykov.

The action follows a March designation of a separate North Korean IT worker network, which Treasury said had laundered roughly $800 million in crypto for the regime. Australia and the European Union have also announced related designations this month, and Treasury coordinated the move with the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team.

Under the sanctions, any property these individuals or entities hold in the United States, or that is controlled by U.S. persons, is blocked and must be reported to the Office of Foreign Assets Control. Transactions with them are generally prohibited unless licensed, and companies owned 50 percent or more by blocked parties are subject to the same restrictions. Treasury warned that civil penalties can apply even when a violation was unintentional.

For companies that hire remote contractors, the advisories from the State, Treasury and Justice departments and the FBI offer guidance on spotting these schemes, including verifying identities, checking where payments are going, and watching for unusual access requests.

Justin Sun’s HTX has agreed to leave the United Kingdom, closing the Financial Conduct Authority’s first enforcement case against a crypto firm over financial promotions. The regulator announced the settlement today, ending a High Court action that began in October 2025, according to Financial Times reporting. 

Under the court undertakings, Huobi Global S.A., the Panama-registered company behind the HTX brand, has promised not to communicate financial promotions that breach UK law across its website, apps and social media channels. 

The FCA says the exchange is no longer active in Britain. UK customers cannot deposit funds, and new users cannot register. Existing customers have 48 hours to withdraw assets before their accounts close.

The regulator framed the outcome as a warning. Steve Smart, the FCA’s executive director of enforcement and market oversight, said that being based overseas does not place a firm beyond the reach of UK law. 

Smart said that ‘Crypto firms should be under no illusion: being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law. Our action means HTX is leaving the UK and can no longer target UK consumers. The message to other firms is clear: follow the rules or face the consequences.’

The regulator said HTX had failed to really engage over several rounds of talks of the case. Settlement talks began in March and were extended in June

HTX settlement and background

HTX presents a different account. The exchange says it has put measures in place to align with UK promotion rules. 

“We take local compliance requirements seriously and have proactively implemented measures to align with the UK’s financial promotion regulations,” the company said in a statement, according to Reuters. 

The settlement terms remain confidential, and the FCA says the deal involves no admission of liability or wrongdoing. Public reporting does not say whether any fine was paid.

In May, the UK sanctioned Huobi Global over alleged support for Russia’s financial sector, listing HTX as another name for the designated entity. 

In July, the European Union named Huobi Global in its 21st Russia sanctions package and barred EU transactions with the exchange, stopping short of a full asset freeze. HTX says Huobi Global S.A. is distinct from the online exchange. 

Back in August, Kraken clients were briefly locked out of their accounts after receiving tiny amounts of cryptocurrency linked to sanctioned funds in what was known as a dust attack. Kraken said the attacks aimed to trigger compliance checks and spread sanctioned funds across platforms, causing operational disruptions for thousands of users. 

Around 12,000 transfers were reportedly sent from a wallet linked to HTX. Kraken’s compliance team quickly restored customer access while retaining the sanctioned funds and working with authorities to prevent further attacks.

title: BNB Chain Jenner Hardfork Hits Testnet With 5% Payment Lane for Faster Crypto Transfers
summary:
Key Takeaways: Now, Jenner has entered the BSC testnet era. The 5% reserved gas for Payment Lane is applicable to eligible payments. The upgrade also adds millisecond timestamps and CAS20
The post BNB Chain Jenner Hardfork Hits Testnet With 5% Payment Lane for Faster Crypto Transfers appeared first ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Now, Jenner has entered the BSC testnet era.
  • The 5% reserved gas for Payment Lane is applicable to eligible payments.
  • The upgrade also adds millisecond timestamps and CAS20 support.

BNB Smart Chain has implemented the Jenner hardfork on its testnet, enabling a specialized payment method to ensure uninterrupted crypto transfers during network congestion. The update includes Payment Lane, more accurate block timestamps and some foundations for the upcoming CAS20 asset standard.

Jenner hardfork is now live on BSC testnet!

What the upgrade entails:
🔸 Payment Lane, reserving 5% of block gas by default for eligible payments.
🔸 Millisecond block timestamps for smart contracts.
🔸 Functionality for CAS20, a new Compliant Asset Standard.

Payment Lane and CAS20 will go through governance before being fully enabled. More details to follow.

Read the full upgrades 👇
https://t.co/pbqJfq7nAD

— BNB Chain (@BNBCHAIN) October 29, 2026

  • BSC Payment Lane Locks 5% of Block Gas for Transfers
  • Stablecoins Need Governance Approval
    • Jenner Adds Millisecond Timing for Smart Contracts
    • CAS20 Expands BNB Chain’s Token Framework

BSC Payment Lane Locks 5% of Block Gas for Transfers

The highlights are Payment Lane, introduced as BEP-703. The default amount of gas the system will place on each block to be used by eligible payment transactions is 5%. The demand for payment doesn’t need to actually be high for general network activity to make use of this reserved capacity.

For example, if a block had a hypothetical 100 million gas limit, 5 million gas would be reserved for payments while general transactions could use up to 95 million. The feature is not a hard limit on payment activity, since under the standard fee rules the remaining block space will be available for eligible payments even if this feature is used.

Read More: Binance Pay Opens Crypto Payments at Millions of PayPay Merchants Across Japan

Stablecoins Need Governance Approval

Not all the tokens transferred are required to be moved to a reserved lane. Regular accounts are eligible for native transfers between accounts, and when a token contract is listed in a list of regulated payments, it is eligible for transfers. The list has no names of the coins and can be supplemented later by the names of the stablecoins or CAS20 coins.

The direct transfer of a stablecoin contract to an approved token contract could be a possibility. If a transaction is sent via a smart contract that isn’t listed, however, it would still be considered general traffic. Governance can also change the amount of the retailer’s capital in a percentage, capped at 10% in the protocol.

Jenner Adds Millisecond Timing for Smart Contracts

Also, the Jenner upgrade will provide smart contracts with a millisecond level of time resolution. Originally, contracts were used with only seconds as time measurements. Applications that require fine time resolution, such as trading systems, quote and short-lived automated DeFi logic, can gain from improved timestability.

BSC blocks value is not increased after the change. Rather, it provides the developers a more accurate indication of the block generation time.

CAS20 Expands BNB Chain’s Token Framework

Jenner also adds CAS20 compliant functionality, also known as Compliant Asset Standard. In addition to traditional BEP-20 tokens, the framework is expected to also support stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets.

Payment Lane and CAS20 are still subject to governance steps to be fully activated, BNB Chain noted. The testnet allows users to test classification of transactions, supported transaction types and integration behavior before they are available in production.

Validators should reject the blocks that don’t obey gas-allocation rules, and any gas allocation rules are reserved with the block builder. It generalises Payment Lane to be integrated into block validation, hence more than a wallet or app option.

title: Understanding the Various Bitcoin Per Share Metrics
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Understanding the Various Bitcoin Per Share Metrics
Bitcoin per share, Bitcoin per assumed diluted shares, Net Bitcoin per share, and what to make of it all.  
This post Understanding the Various Bitcoin Per Share Metrics first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Allard ...
content:
Bitcoin per share is one of the most important metrics for evaluating a Bitcoin treasury company. It measures how much bitcoin is attributable to each common share. However, there are several ways to calculate this figure, and each method provides different information about the economics of owning the common stock.

Understanding these differences is essential for evaluating a company’s capital structure, measuring accretion, and determining the value attributable to common shareholders.

Raw Bitcoin Per Share

The simplest metric is raw Bitcoin Per Share (BPS).

BPS = Total Bitcoin Holdings / Common Shares Outstanding

This calculation divides the company’s bitcoin holdings by its existing common shares. It provides a straightforward measure of how much bitcoin is attributable to each currently outstanding share.

The primary limitation is its treatment of potential dilution. A company may have warrants, convertible debt, or convertible preferred stock that could eventually become common shares. Raw BPS only counts existing shares, so it provides an incomplete picture of the potential future share count.

Bitcoin Per Assumed Diluted Share

Bitcoin Per Assumed Diluted Share (BPADS) addresses this limitation by incorporating the shares that would exist if all potentially dilutive securities converted into common stock.

BPADS = Total Bitcoin Holdings / Assumed Diluted Shares Outstanding

Because the assumed diluted share count is greater than or equal to the existing share count, BPADS is always less than or equal to raw BPS.

This metric became widely cited beginning in 2024, particularly as Bitcoin treasury companies began using increasingly complex capital structures.

BPADS provides a more conservative view of bitcoin ownership by incorporating potential dilution from outstanding securities. It becomes especially relevant for companies with substantial convertible debt, warrants, or convertible preferred stock.

However, its assumption of full conversion can be overly conservative.

Warrants and convertible debt may never convert if the common stock price remains below their conversion or exercise prices. Perpetual convertible preferred stock may also remain outstanding indefinitely if investors prefer receiving the preferred dividend rather than converting into common equity.

Consequently, BPADS represents a fully diluted scenario rather than a forecast of the actual future share count.

Net Bitcoin Per Share

Both BPS and BPADS share another major limitation: they measure gross bitcoin holdings without accounting for senior claims on the company’s assets.

Common equity sits at the bottom of the capital structure. Debt holders and preferred shareholders generally have priority over common shareholders according to their contractual rights.

These senior claims matter because they reduce the assets ultimately attributable to common equity.

Net Bitcoin Per Share (Net BPS) addresses this by deducting the bitcoin equivalent of senior claims from total bitcoin holdings before dividing by the common share count.

The basic calculation is:

Net BPS = (Total Bitcoin Holdings − Senior Claims / Bitcoin Price) / Common Shares

For example, a company with $1 billion in senior claims and a bitcoin price of $100,000 would need the equivalent of 10,000 bitcoin to satisfy those claims.

Those 10,000 bitcoin would therefore be deducted from gross bitcoin holdings when calculating Net BPS.

The denominator can use either existing common shares or an assumed diluted share count. However, the treatment must remain consistent: securities assumed to convert into common stock should have their extinguished senior claims removed from the numerator’s deductions. This avoids counting the same obligation twice.

Should cash be included?

There are two useful approaches to calculating Net BPS.

The first applies cash and cash equivalents against senior claims before deducting the remaining obligations from bitcoin holdings.

Net BPS = [Bitcoin Holdings − (Senior Claims − Applied Cash) / Bitcoin Price] / Common Shares

Here, applied cash is limited to the amount available to offset senior claims. This method reflects the fact that cash can satisfy obligations, preserving more bitcoin for common shareholders. This is the methodology used by Strategy to compute their mNAV. 

The second approach deducts the full value of senior claims from bitcoin holdings and reports cash separately. For example, investors could examine both Net BPS and Cash Per Share. This separation provides a clearer view of the company’s bitcoin exposure alongside its independent cash reserves, at a per-share level.

Both approaches are useful. Including cash produces a more comprehensive measure of residual asset value, while excluding cash makes the company’s bitcoin and cash positions separately visible.

Net BPS changes with bitcoin’s price

A defining characteristic of Net BPS is its sensitivity to the price of bitcoin.

Raw BPS and BPADS depend on bitcoin holdings and share counts. Net BPS additionally depends on bitcoin’s market price because senior claims are generally denominated in dollars.

As bitcoin appreciates, fewer bitcoins are required to cover a fixed dollar obligation, so more bitcoins remain attributable to common shareholders. When bitcoin depreciates, the opposite occurs.

Net BPS therefore rises with bitcoin’s price and falls when bitcoin’s price declines, assuming fixed senior claims, holdings, and share counts.

This relationship creates both a challenge and an important advantage.

Challenge: Measuring accretion correctly

The challenge is that changes in Net BPS over time combine the effects of corporate actions with changes in bitcoin’s market price.

A rising bitcoin price can increase Net BPS even when a company’s financing decisions destroy value for common shareholders. Conversely, falling bitcoin prices can obscure the benefits of genuinely accretive transactions.

This makes directly comparing observed Net BPS figures across different dates an unreliable method of evaluating management’s capital allocation decisions.

However, raw BPS and BPADS are also inadequate measures of economic accretion.

Consider a company issuing debt to purchase bitcoin. Any positive amount of bitcoin purchased with debt increases raw BPS because bitcoin holdings rise while common shares remain unchanged. This holds regardless of the debt’s interest rate or repayment obligations.

Similarly, issuing preferred stock to purchase bitcoin increases raw BPS even if the preferred stock is issued at a substantial discount to par and carries expensive dividend obligations.

These transactions increase gross bitcoin ownership per common share while potentially reducing the residual value attributable to common shareholders.

The proper way to measure economic accretion is to compare Net BPS before and after a transaction while holding the bitcoin price constant.

This isolates the effects of changes in bitcoin holdings, senior claims, cash, and share count.

It reveals whether a corporate action genuinely increases the bitcoin equivalent of the residual assets attributable to each common share.

Advantage: Net BPS as a measure of common equity liquidation value

Perhaps the greatest advantage of Net BPS is its connection to the economic value of common equity. When bitcoin is a company’s primary treasury asset, Net BPS calculated with the appropriate cash adjustment approximates the bitcoin denominated liquidation value attributable to each common share. 

(Note: by liquidation value, I mean the value that common stockholders would be entitled to if they liquidated the company, paid off all the claims, and divided the remainder amongst themselves. This has nothing to do with the “liquidation value” associated with leveraged, margin-callable trading positions. Actual recoveries in a real liquidation depend on the precise terms of senior securities, other assets and liabilities, liquidation expenses, and the taxable proceeds realized from asset sales.) 

Multiplying Net BPS by the bitcoin price converts this amount into dollars. Investors can then compare that dollar figure with the common stock’s market price to measure the premium or discount at which the shares trade relative to their estimated residual asset value. 

This is an advantage that BPS and BPADS cannot offer. Because Net BPS accounts for senior claims, it provides a more direct measure of the assets that ultimately belong to common shareholders, making it the most relevant basis for comparison with the common stock’s market price.

This connection to common equity liquidation value also explains why accretion is best measured through changes in Net BPS at a constant bitcoin price. Holding the price constant isolates the impact of corporate actions on the residual asset value attributable to each common share. And because Net BPS factors in both senior claims and common stock, it accounts for the impact of all possible corporate actions that involve issuance or repurchase of securities interests, while projecting the results of the impact onto the common stock. 

Conclusion

Each Bitcoin per share metric serves a distinct purpose.

Raw BPS measures gross bitcoin holdings attributable to existing common shares. BPADS incorporates potential dilution. Net BPS accounts for senior claims and measures the residual bitcoin value attributable to common equity.

For evaluating the capital stack, Net BPS is the most comprehensive of the three. Holding bitcoin’s price constant allows investors to isolate the economic effects of financing transactions and assess genuine accretion. Net BPS provides a direct connection between the company’s balance sheet and the market value of its common stock.

Tradeweb Markets reported third-quarter revenue of $584.5 million today (Thursday), up 14.9% from a year earlier. Average daily volume across its bond, swap, equity and money market platforms rose 22.4% to $3.15 trillion, the company said.
The results are the first since Tradeweb agreed on October 1...
content:
2026-10-29T14:44:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 12:44 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Interest rate swaps and government bonds led the quarter, lifting the rates business 18.2% to $324.5 million.
  • Net income rose 6.8% as other income halved, including a $24 million paper loss on its crypto token holdings.

Tradeweb Markets reported third-quarter revenue of $584.5 million today (Thursday), up 14.9% from a year earlier. Average daily volume across its bond, swap, equity and money market platforms rose 22.4% to $3.15 trillion, the company said.

The results are the first since Tradeweb agreed on October 19 to buy bond trading venue Trumid for about $1.97 billion, three months after Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) agreed to take over MarketAxess for about $5.7 billion.

Tradeweb ended September with $2.1 billion in cash and plans to fund the $1.89 billion cash part of the deal mainly from that balance.

Net income grew more slowly than revenue, rising 6.8% to $224.9 million, as other income fell to $18.7 million from $39.4 million. Adjusted net income, which leaves those items out, rose 15.6% to $238.8 million.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Growth Picked Up After a Slower Second Quarter

Set against its own year, the third quarter put Tradeweb's growth rate between the two before it. Revenue rose 21.2% to $617.8 million in the first quarter, when volume hit a record, and 9% to $558.9 million in the second.

Over nine months, revenue came to $1.76 billion, up 15.0% from the same period of 2025, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from the company's figures.

Rates trading brought in $324.5 million, up 18.2% and more than half of group revenue. Average daily volume in rates derivatives rose 46.0% to $1.35 trillion, with swaps and swaptions of one year or longer up 42.4%.

Tradeweb tied the swaps activity to central bank policy changes, geopolitical tension and uncertainty over inflation. US government bond volume rose 28.0%, and September was the busiest month of the year for Treasury trading on Tradeweb, when total daily volume rose 33.7% to $3.74 trillion.

Fees did not keep pace with volume. Average variable fees per million on long-dated rates derivatives fell 10.5%, which the company put down to more compression trades and shorter duration.

Credit Share Rose Under a New Reporting Rule

Credit revenue rose 9.6% to $133.0 million, while US credit volume grew 23.9%. Average variable fees per million in cash credit fell 10.6% as trading shifted toward portfolio trades, which carry a lower fee, the company said.

Tradeweb's share of fully electronic US high-grade bond volume reported to TRACE reached 19.9%, up 1.3 percentage points from a year earlier and above the 17.5% it held in January.

Part of that gain reflects a reporting change. From August 31, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) excluded certain duplicate trades between affiliates from TRACE, which lowered reported market volume and raised Tradeweb's share.

Earlier periods were not restated, so the figures may not be comparable, Tradeweb said.

Credit derivatives volume rose 61.3% as hedge funds and systematic accounts traded more credit default swaps on its swap execution and multilateral trading facilities, a business that overtook cash credit on Tradeweb in July.

Trumid would be "the largest acquisition in our history," Billy Hult, CEO of Tradeweb, said in the results statement.

The target's average daily volume rose 38% to $9.6 billion in the third quarter. The deal needs regulatory approval and is targeted to close in the first half of 2027, and Tradeweb's updated 2026 guidance leaves it out.

Canton Coin Loss and $210 Million in Buybacks

Other income included a $27.5 million gain booked when Tradeweb converted a note in tokenization firm Securitize into shares on July 1, and a $14.4 million gain on a minority investment. A $24.0 million unrealized loss on its Canton Coin holdings offset part of that.

Tradeweb held 1.6 billion of the crypto tokens at the end of September, valued at $207.5 million. It cannot freely transfer 1.3 billion of them, worth $163.7 million. Revenue from validating transactions on the Canton Network fell, pulling the "other" revenue line down 17.3% to $7.6 million.

Its investments outside core trading also include a minority stake in prediction market operator Kalshi taken in February, and in October it joined a $220 million financing round for Capitolis.

Taker volume at Kalshi and Polymarket's two venues reached $172.4 billion in the third quarter, against $98.5 billion in the second, according to FM Intelligence calculations.

Operating expenses rose 11.0% to $331.1 million. Tradeweb revised its full-year adjusted expense guidance to $1.155 billion to $1.175 billion, citing revenue growth so far this year, and said spending was trending toward the middle of that range.

The company bought back 2.02 million shares for $209.8 million during the quarter, at an average of $103.83, leaving $124.5 million under its authorization. It declared a quarterly dividend of $0.14 per share, up 16.7%, payable on December 15.

title: Alpaca Joins JPMorgan and Citadel Securities as US Settlement Hub Starts Tokenizing Stocks
summary:
US broker-dealer Alpaca is one of 20 firms that signed up for the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's (DTCC) tokenization service, which went live yesterday (Wednesday). It lets them turn US stocks, ETFs and Treasuries held at the depository into tokens and back.
Tokenized stocks that pass thr...
content:
2026-10-29T14:26:51.228+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 12:26 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The broker-dealer is among 20 firms that signed up for the DTCC service at its launch on Wednesday.
  • Robinhood, Schwab and Interactive Brokers were not among them, though more firms will join on a rolling basis.

US broker-dealer Alpaca is one of 20 firms that signed up for the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation's (DTCC) tokenization service, which went live yesterday (Wednesday). It lets them turn US stocks, ETFs and Treasuries held at the depository into tokens and back.

Tokenized stocks that pass through Alpaca's network are issued by third parties. They generally give economic exposure without voting or dividend rights, according to the company's risk disclosure.

DTCC says its tokens keep the ownership rights and investor protections of the securities it holds, a pool worth more than $114 trillion.

The launch follows a December 2025 no-action letter from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and test trades with more than 30 firms in July. The SEC separately approved a Nasdaq pilot in March for trading tokenized Russell 1000 stocks alongside ordinary shares.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Kraken and Robinhood Are Not on the List

Firms already active in tokenized US stocks split on DTCC's launch lists. Ondo and DRW, both early partners of Alpaca's tokenization network, appear among the collaborators DTCC named, alongside BitGo, Fireblocks and Tradeweb.

Kraken, whose xStocks passed $25 billion in cumulative volume within eight months, is on neither list, and neither is eToro, which announced tokenized US shares in October 2025. Robinhood, which sells stock tokens in the European Union, is also absent.

Of the six firms named here, three made DTCC's lists, with Alpaca the only one signed up as a participant.

Alpaca's Part in the July Trades

Alpaca joined DTCC's industry working group in May. In July, it said, it helped partners tokenize SPY and Circle shares held at the depository on the Canton Network and DTCC's private Besu network, then redeem them through its own system.

That system is the Instant Tokenization Network, which Alpaca launched in October 2025 to let institutions swap shares for tokens in kind. The company said several partners now use it to mint and redeem tokenized US equities.

Alpaca said tokenized US equities scale "when traditional markets and onchain markets share the same foundation."

One of its backers is now a fellow participant. Citadel Securities took part in the $150 million round that valued Alpaca at $1.15 billion in January and also signed up for the DTCC service.

The rest of the list runs from J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and UBS to clearing firms Apex Clearing, Clear Street and DriveWealth. Among retail brokers, Fidelity Investments and Edward Jones signed up, while Charles Schwab and Interactive Brokers are not among the 20.

Eligible assets at launch are Russell 1000 constituents, ETFs tracking major indices and US Treasury securities. DTCC said it will onboard more participants on a rolling basis and plans to add blockchain networks in 2027.

One of its backers is now a fellow participant. Citadel Securities took part in the $150 million round that valued Alpaca at $1.15 billion in January and also signed up for the DTCC service.

The rest of the list runs from J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley and UBS to clearing firms Apex Clearing, Clear Street and DriveWealth. Among retail brokers, Fidelity Investments and Edward Jones signed up, while Charles Schwab and Interactive Brokers are not among the 20.

Eligible assets at launch are Russell 1000 constituents, ETFs tracking major indices and US Treasury securities. DTCC said it will onboard more participants on a rolling basis and plans to add blockchain networks in 2027.

title: Travala Unveils AVA+ Partners, a New Route to Crypto Payments Powered by AVA
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 29th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 29th October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 29th, 2026, Chainwire

Crypto projects will be able to lock AVA to have their token accepted as payment on Travala.

Travala, the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, today announced AVA+ Partners, a new program that will provide crypto projects with a route to having their token accepted as a payment method on Travala by buying and locking AVA, the token at the heart of the Travala ecosystem.

The program, which is currently in development, will require partner projects to hold AVA for as long as their token is accepted on Travala while receiving partner rewards throughout the partnership.

AVA+ Partners involves three steps for crypto partner projects:

  1. Buy AVA. Partner projects acquire AVA on the open market.
  2. Buy NFT. Partner projects acquire a Travel Tiger NFT.
  3. Activate & Lock. Partner projects activate a Smart Diamond membership and lock AVA in a dedicated AVA+ Partners smart contract for as long as the project’s token is accepted on Travala.

Projects can withdraw from AVA+ Partners at any time. Those that leave the program early contribute part of their locked AVA to the AVA Strategic Reserve, which Travala has committed never to sell or transfer from. All partner projects are subject to Travala’s approval.

“AVA+ Partners turns real-world utility on Travala into a long-term commitment to AVA,” said Steve Hipwell, AVA Foundation Lead Contributor. “It’s a use case that grows directly with the expansion of our partner and payment ecosystem.”

The initiative is the latest in a string of joint Travala and AVA ecosystem announcements. AVA locked in AVA+ Partners builds towards the recently announced long-term goal of achieving 30% of AVA’s circulating supply locked, with AVA locked by partner projects counted alongside AVA locked through the AVA Smart Program and AVA+ Rewards. Full terms, including withdrawal fees, will be set out in each partner agreement.

Projects interested in becoming partners can contact [email protected].

Disclaimer

AVA+ Partners is offered to approved business partners only, under individual agreements, and may be modified or discontinued. This announcement is for information only; it is not an offer, solicitation or inducement to acquire, hold or lock AVA, and is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates or any jurisdiction where distribution would be unlawful. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies.

About Travala

Founded in 2017 and now backed by industry giant Binance, Travala is the leading crypto-native travel booking service, offering 2,200,000+ properties across 230 countries, 600+ airlines, 50,000+ car rental locations, and 400,000+ activities globally. Travala is a champion of cryptocurrency adoption, accepting over 100 leading cryptocurrencies alongside traditional payment methods. For more information, visit: www.travala.com.

About the AVA Foundation

The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org.

Contact

Lead Contributor
Steve Hipwell
AVA Foundation

title: Crypto Exchange HTX Leaves UK and Settles Regulator’s Lawsuit Over Illegal Ads
summary:
HTX, the crypto exchange formerly known as Huobi, has settled a lawsuit brought by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and left the UK market. The regulator said today (Thursday) that HTX gave court undertakings not to knowingly promote its services to UK consumers.
The case was the first the FCA ...
content:
2026-10-29T13:11:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 11:11 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The former Huobi gave court undertakings not to knowingly promote its services to British consumers.
  • Users there can no longer deposit, and the confidential terms carry no admission of liability.

HTX, the crypto exchange formerly known as Huobi, has settled a lawsuit brought by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and left the UK market. The regulator said today (Thursday) that HTX gave court undertakings not to knowingly promote its services to UK consumers.

The case was the first the FCA brought against a crypto firm for marketing to UK consumers since crypto came under the financial promotion rules in October 2023.

Most of the regulator's work against illegal ads stays out of court. It flagged nearly 20,000 financial promotions in 2024, almost double the year before.

London's trading industry is coming home!

HTX is no longer active in the UK, the FCA said. British users can no longer deposit funds, new UK customers cannot sign up, and the exchange has committed not to target, solicit or actively seek UK consumers on its website, apps or social media.

A Year in the High Court

The FCA sued HTX in the High Court in London in October 2025, naming Panama-incorporated Huobi Global S.A. and several groups of unidentified people who run the exchange and its accounts on X, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram, TikTok, YouTube, Discord, Medium and LinkedIn.

When it made the case public in February, the regulator asked social media companies to block HTX's accounts for UK users and asked Apple and Google to pull its apps from their UK stores. The FCA said HTX repeatedly failed to engage before moving to leave the UK.

Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said crypto firms should be "under no illusion" that "being based overseas does not put them beyond the reach of UK law."

The settlement sits in a Tomlin order dated Tuesday. Its terms are confidential and are not an admission of liability or wrongdoing by Huobi Global or anyone else, the FCA said. It pointed remaining UK users to HTX's website for instructions on withdrawing their assets.

The regulator's more routine tool is its warning list, which names firms it suspects of operating without permission. FM Intelligence's fines and warnings tracker logged 240 warnings in the UK in the 30 days to October 28.

Sanctions Added to the Pressure

The court case was not the only pressure on HTX this year. In May, the UK sanctioned the exchange along with 17 other crypto businesses it described as part of networks supporting Russia's economy, and the European Union added HTX to its Russia sanctions list in July.

Binance stopped processing transactions with HTX and 10 other platforms from August 23, citing regulatory developments. HTX has disputed that the UK designation covers its exchange.

Justin Sun took a controlling stake in the exchange in 2022, and HTX describes him as an adviser. It dropped the Huobi name in 2023, the same year it saw $258 million flow out after a cyberattack.

FinanceMagnates.com has sent questions to HTX about the settlement and its remaining UK users and will update this article if HTX responds.

What a Return Would Take

Serving UK users legally again would mean passing an FCA review that most crypto applicants have not cleared. The regulator opened its authorization window for crypto firms on September 30.

Applications filed by February 28, 2027 will be assessed before the new regime starts on October 25, 2027, and existing registrations will not convert into authorizations automatically.

Under the current anti-money laundering registration regime, 68 of 391 completed crypto applications between January 2020 and August 1, 2026 ended in registration, FM Intelligence data show. Another 263 were withdrawn.

That puts the registration rate at 17% for the full period, rising to 56% in the latest 12 months on 23 decisions.

title: Lagarde’s ECB Era, From Pandemic to 4% Rates, Ends Nine Months Early
summary:
Christine Lagarde will step down early as president of the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank said today (Thursday). Her seven years in the job took in a pandemic, record euro area inflation and 10 straight rate hikes.

content:
2026-10-29T12:52:49.099+02:00

Thursday, 29/10/2026 | 10:52 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Her last day is February 7, 2027, and EU leaders must now choose who takes over the central bank.
  • Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos and Dutch central banker Klaas Knot are reported frontrunners for the job.

Christine Lagarde will step down early as president of the European Central Bank (ECB), the central bank said today (Thursday). Her seven years in the job took in a pandemic, record euro area inflation and 10 straight rate hikes.

Her last day will be February 7, 2027, almost nine months before her eight-year term ends. The Governing Council thanked her with a long standing ovation, according to the ECB, and the European Council will now appoint her successor.

The exit lands mid-cycle for euro traders. The deposit rate stands at 2.50% after quarter-point increases in June and September, and futures pricing points to another rise in December.

London's trading industry is coming home!

A Pandemic Four Months In

Lagarde became the first woman to lead the ECB on November 1, 2019. A lawyer and former French finance minister, she had also swum for France's national synchronized swimming team as a teenager.

She took over from Mario Draghi, whose ECB had pushed the deposit rate further below zero in a split vote in 2014. Covid-19 reached Europe four months into her term.

At her first crisis press conference, on March 12, 2020, she said the ECB was "not here to close spreads."

Italy's 10-year bond yield climbed more than 60 basis points that day, and Lagarde walked the comment back in a CNBC interview hours later. Retail traders piled in that month, and GAIN Capital clients alone traded $388.6 billion in March 2020, up 95% from February.

On March 18, six days after that press conference, the ECB launched a EUR 750 billion pandemic emergency purchase program, which grew to EUR 1.85 trillion by December 2020.

Ten Hikes to a Record 4%

The deposit rate stayed at -0.50% through the pandemic, in a regime where the bank had once even weighed paying banks to take its long-term loans.

Then annual euro area inflation reached 10.6% in October 2022. The ECB raised rates 10 times in a row from July 2022, and by September 2023 the deposit rate stood at 4.00%, the highest since the euro's launch in 1999.

Eight cuts between June 2024 and June 2025 brought it back to 2.00%, before energy prices pushed the bank into hiking again this year. The euro area meanwhile grew from 19 to 21 members, with Croatia joining in 2023 and Bulgaria in January 2026.

One promise is still open. In November 2020 Lagarde said the ECB would likely launch a digital euro within two to four years. Six years later, the European Parliament has only just voted, in July, to open talks with member states on the law.

The ECB's case rests on how Europeans pay. Only 24% of euro area retail payments were made in cash in 2023, according to figures the ECB cited last year, and the bank now points to 2029 as the earliest issuance date.

Three Board Seats Open in Five Months

Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel leaves on January 3 to join the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and chief economist Philip Lane's term ends in May.

Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot have been named in reports as the main candidates for the presidency. The earlier exit also gives French President Emmanuel Macron a say before France elects his successor in the spring.

Lagarde will be the first ECB president since Wim Duisenberg, who left in 2003, to step down before completing an eight-year term.

title: MetaMask, Trezor, WalletConnect and Other Industry Leaders Join ChangeNOW at TOKEN2049
summary: Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 29th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 29th October 2026, Chainwire

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, October 28th, 2026, Chainwire

ChangeNOW’s TOKEN2049 Singapore program featured four panel discussions with speakers from MetaMask, Trezor, WalletConnect, and other projects, a series of NOW Effect interviews, and a keynote by Chief Strategy Officer Pauline Shangett.

In her Bit Digital Stage talk, “Next Billion Users Should Never Touch Blockchain,” Shangett argued that people should be able to use crypto without choosing networks, managing gas or navigating separate services. She presented crypto super apps as a way to bring everyday financial tasks into one product.

At the ChangeNOW booth, The Block’s Kelvin Sparks moderated a wallet panel with MetaMask, Trezor and ChangeNOW. Speakers discussed how wallets are expanding as more services move into a single interface, alongside security and user approval for AI agents.

“The user shouldn’t have to think about gas. The user shouldn’t have to go through multiple steps to switch from one network to another, when a lot of that can be done in the background,” said Yana, Head of Business Development & Account Management at ChangeNOW.

The infrastructure session brought together Banxa, RocketX, WalletConnect and Aztec Labs to discuss transaction routing, privacy for on-chain payments and collaboration amongst specialized providers.

A panel on crypto super apps including Pulsar Money, Rubic, Hercules and CoinRoutes debated whether payments, trading or a broader variety of financial services would give consumers a reason to return regularly. Shangett identified payments as one potential foundation for these apps.

The fourth panel featured CoinEasy, The Block of Media and ChangeNOW. Speakers examined AI’s impact on search, SEO and audience monetization, discussing communities, podcasts and video, as well as opportunities to integrate crypto swaps into media and analytics platforms.

Journalist Ramia Farrage hosted NOW Effect interviews with representatives of Stellar, Injective, NEAR Intents, USDD, Sonic and Zcash. The conversations covered cross-border payments, institutional participation in DeFi, stablecoins, privacy and blockchain usability.

The panels and interviews were recorded for release as part of ChangeNOW’s TOKEN2049 coverage. Further highlights from the event are available in the company’s Day 1 and Day 2 recaps.

About ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW.io is a crypto super app built for every crypto move, giving newcomers, professionals, and businesses the tools they need to access Web3 finance in a simple and secure way.

Since 2017, ChangeNOW has grown from a fast, secure, and limitless instant exchange into a trusted platform where storage, swaps, trading, staking, and asset management are covered in one simple experience for millions of clients worldwide.

title: Kraken USDC Jumps 30% While EURC Trading Nears 1B in Circle Stablecoin Expansion
summary:
Key Takeaways: USDC on Kraken trading volume increased over 30% in a 1-year time period. Kraken has traded nearly 1 billion EURC since it listed. DeFi Earn by Kraken has
The post Kraken USDC Jumps 30% While EURC Trading Nears 1B in Circle Stablecoin Expansion appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • USDC on Kraken trading volume increased over 30% in a 1-year time period.
  • Kraken has traded nearly 1 billion EURC since it listed.
  • DeFi Earn by Kraken has over $350 Million worth of USDC deposits.

Circle says its stablecoin partnership with Kraken is producing measurable growth across trading, funding and onchain products.

Stablecoins are moving deeper into the products customers already use.

Kraken partnered with Circle to expand USDC and EURC utility across funding, trading, wallet infrastructure, and onchain access.

The results:

→ 30% USDC AUC growth on Kraken since its September 2025 partnership with Circle
→ Nearly 1B EURC traded on Kraken since listing
→ 350M USDC deposited to Kraken’s DeFi Earn vaults post launch

For Kraken, building with USDC and EURC helped reduce fragmentation across core platform flows and give customers more direct access to dollar- and euro-denominated stablecoin utility.

https://t.co/Qxaxgtoz6S

— Circle (@circle) October 28, 2026

The companies’ partnership has since widened in September 2025, and USDC volume on Kraken has risen by over 30% while EURC has grown into a large trading market in euros.

  • Kraken Pushes USDC Beyond Spot Trading
  • DeFi Earn Pulls in $350M of USDC
    • EURC Trading Approaches 1 Billion on Kraken
    • Circle and Kraken Turn Stablecoins Into Core Infrastructure

Kraken Pushes USDC Beyond Spot Trading

In 2020, Kraken already had ties with USDC, but in 2025, it will extend the token into the exchange’s infrastructure through a partnership with Circle.

Rather than just using USDC as a trading pair, Kraken translated its funding, earn offerings, wallet infrastructure and onchain applications to this pair. Circle aimed to provide fewer conversion steps and more direct access for users to convert to the $ in order to arbitrate.

The strategy seems like it’s starting to succeed. According to Circle, USDC on Kraken has risen by over 30% since September of 2025 to September of 2026. As of October 26, Circle says that it has approximately $71 billion worth of USDC in circulation, and approximately $71.2 billion worth of reserve denominated in USDC.

Read More: Circle Brings USDC and EURC Into SAP Workflows Powering 84% of Global Commerce

DeFi Earn Pulls in $350M of USDC

The most obvious one is arguably the DeFi Earn product of Kraken. Eligible assets deposited by customers can be converted into USDC, moved through an embedded wallet and allocated into Veda vaults on Ink, Kraken-supported Ethereum Layer 2 infrastructure built on the Optimism stack.

They are able to connect with third-party lending protocols such as Aave, while risk managers are independent thus managing liquidity and allocations. In the months after the launch, over $350 million worth of USDC was deposited into Circle’s DeFi Earn vaults.

EURC Trading Approaches 1 Billion on Kraken

Kraken also launched its € stablecoin launch with the addition of EURC in September 2025. Under the MiCA framework in Europe, the token will offer them an alternative trading option that’s denominated in euros, as well as account funding and collateral.

According to Circle, EURC’s on-chain volume has increased from almost 4 million tokens in October 2025 to over 75 million tokens by September 2026. In some months, over 100 million EURC worth of trading has been recorded; in total, trading since the listing has been close to 1 billion EURC.

Circle and Kraken Turn Stablecoins Into Core Infrastructure

The partnership has announced a bigger trend towards the adoption of stablecoins among exchanges. Settlement and liquidity infrastructure have developed much more quickly for USDC and EURC than they have for the dollars and euros that are traded, settled, and created.

For Kraken, the double token approach from a single issuer will minimize the need to coordinate between multiple stablecoin issuers regarding funding, trading and onchain processes. According to Circle, this has helped cut down on fragmentations and foster access to liquidity in dollars and euros.

It is also a part of USDC’s activity that is being scaled in crypto markets. Throughout the first half of 2026, Circle crossed USDC onchain transaction volume of over $36 trillion, highlighting how stablecoins are now becoming a mainstay of exchange and settlement infrastructure.

  • Trading Works More Like a Token Swap
    • CFTC Relief Cleared Phantom’s Route Into Regulated Markets
    • Prediction Markets Become a New Crypto Wallet Battleground

Phantom Adds Kalshi Prediction Markets Inside Its Crypto Wallet

The new experience, Predict, lets Phantom users wager on events without needing to leave its application. Kalshi is a CFTC registered exchange that performs customer verification, keeps trading accounts and carries out trades placed by customers. The software that’s connecting users through those markets is Phantom.Phantom is the software connecting users to those markets.

Initially, markets will include crypto, pro/college sports, economics, politics, AI and other up-to-the-minute events. One of the harsher offers is short-term Bitcoin pricing markets, such as contracts that might settle each 15 minutes, for crypto traders. This results in Phantom users having a format that’s much closer to the fast trading style that already exists in crypto markets.

Read More: NBA Taps Kalshi and Polymarket in Prediction Markets Deal With CFTC Safeguards

Trading Works More Like a Token Swap

Phantom details the interface to be familiar to current wallet customers. Predictions can be covered with Phantom cash, and when they are fulfilled, the cash goes back on Phantoms. Phantom’s support documentation indicates that trades that are funded from a Cash account are gasless as well.

The markets feature live pricing, a feed of event data and a chat room where users can view sentiment as contract odds change. Existing Kalshi users can join their existing accounts or new users need to go through Kalshi’s identity verification process before they are able to trade.

CFTC Relief Cleared Phantom’s Route Into Regulated Markets

The launch is an outgrowth of a regulatory effort Phantom has already undertaken this year. CFTC’s Market Participants Division issued Staff Letter 26-09 on March 17, which postpones the implementation of broker registration requirements for certain activity until Phantom gets more specific.

Phantom is relieved about the ability to provide its self-custodial software solution to enable users to trade with registered derivatives market makers and exchanges without serving as a broker. Phantom later claimed it’s the first passive software provider to be granted such relief.

Prediction Markets Become a New Crypto Wallet Battleground

The Kalshi integration allows Phantom to grow beyond trading tokens and the wallet tagging to event-based markets.

This change is significant, as the speed at which prices move, their holding time, and the round-the-clock trading in such markets are becoming more aligned with crypto user habits.

Still limited availability in some areas. U.S. Kalshi prediction markets are not available in Michigan, Nevada and Washington, and some categories of contracts may be subject to further state restrictions, Phantom says.

The approach with Phantom is evolving into a future where trading poker, existing trading or anything else on the blockchain is conducted entirely within the app.

title: Netflix Revives FTX’s $8B Collapse With SBF Prison Emails and The Altruists Drama
summary:
Key Takeaways: Anthony Boyle met Sam Bankman-Fried in prison before he was cast as the main character in The Altruists. The eight-episode Netflix series is about the failure of FTX’s
The post Netflix Revives FTX’s $8B Collapse With SBF Prison Emails and The Altruists Drama appeared first on CryptoNi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Anthony Boyle met Sam Bankman-Fried in prison before he was cast as the main character in The Altruists.
  • The eight-episode Netflix series is about the failure of FTX’s $8 billion, the crash of SBF and Caroline Ellison.
  • Bankman-Fried has received a 25-year prison term for fraud and conspiracy.

Since that time, the FTX drama is coming back into the limelight with Netflix’s new eight episode long drama, The Altruists. Prior to the 19 release in November, actor Anthony Boyle has indicated that he was speaking to the former FTX chief before being cast as an actor portraying him in the film.

Read More: Netflix Revives FTX’s $8B Scandal in ‘The Altruists’ With SBF and Caroline Ellison

  • Anthony Boyle Contacted SBF From Prison Before Filming
  • Netflix Focuses on SBF and Caroline Ellison
    • FTX’s Collapse Still Defines One of Crypto’s Biggest Frauds
    • The Altruists Turns Crypto’s Biggest Scandal Into Character Drama

Anthony Boyle Contacted SBF From Prison Before Filming

Boyle told Vanity Fair that he reached out to Bankman-Fried while researching the role and sent him more than 100 questions. Many of them answered them, but Boyle didn’t reveal anything because he had promised to keep the correspondence private, said the actor.

Instead of the mechanics, his interest lay in what propelled Bankman-Fried to its position. Boyle said he wanted to know what made somebody one of the youngest billionaires in the world and how ambition, ideology and ego influenced his decisions.

Netflix Focuses on SBF and Caroline Ellison

The Altruists cast Boyle as Altruist’s CEO Bankman-Fried, while Julia Garner plays Caroline Ellison, who was the CEO at Alameda Research.

According to Netflix, the two young idealists succeeded in changing the financial system before being caught up in an alleged $8 billion fraud. The series takes inspiration from New York magazine articles, and is set to premiere Nov. 19.

In contrast to a focus on the financial scandal of FTX, the trailer frames it as an empire and as a personal fascination of SBF and Ellison.

FTX’s Collapse Still Defines One of Crypto’s Biggest Frauds

In March 2024, he was convicted on seven criminal charges, including wire fraud, securities fraud conspiracy, commodities fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy, and sentenced to 25 years in prison.

He embezzled billions of dollars of FTX customer assets, defrauded investors of over $1.7 billion, and defrauded Alameda lenders of over $1.3 billion, U.S. prosecutors said. One of the more harmful happenings in crypto history, the FTX collapse is still notable, as the exchange was previously thought of as a big trading platform worldwide.

The Altruists Turns Crypto’s Biggest Scandal Into Character Drama

Instead of just showing Bankman-Fried as a disgraced crypto-entrepreneur, Boyle said the show’s focus is on his insecurity, anxiety, and belief in effective altruism. That way, Netflix has the freedom to look back on the collision between idealism, risk-taking and individual ambition within FTX.

Boyle also stressed that the story is not just about eccentric founders or tech culture. The real world financial effects of the collapse were suffered by customers and investors, with the drama intricately entangled in one of crypto’s most significant failures.
